docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera
docs.t: Asked for after the Vivobook tests: installation wizards for apps downloaded as files (built in 1.5.6, before 1.5.5's remaining items), and the Vivobook's camera.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera › What is there today (checked in the code and on the Vivobook)
docs.t: .deb: opening one says that Rudolf OS does not install packages from a file yet, and offers the App Store (#128). Debian 13 runs beside Rudolf OS (rudolf-debian, its own namespaces); Settings › Apps › Linux sets it up, updates it and installs Wine. .exe and .msi: they open with Wine when Wine is installed (1.4.8, 1.4.9). There is no wizard: the installer just runs, and what it installs shows up in the Start menu by itself. .AppImage, .bin, .apk, .ipa: nothing opens them.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera › What is there today (checked in the code and on the Vivobook)
docs.t: Debian and your folders: Debian's programs, Wine included, did not see the account's folders as 1.5.6 has them, and with "Encrypt my data" they could not open Downloads at all (fixed in #137, needed by every wizard below). The camera: the kernel finds the Vivobook's webcam (a USB webcam, UVC, 3277:0034), but its device was the system's only, so no app could open it (fixed in #136).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera › The wizard (all file types)
docs.t: Opening an installable file in File Explorer or from Oracle's Downloads opens Install <name>, one window with the same steps for every type: 1. What it is: the app's name, version, publisher and size where the file says (a .deb's control fields, an .exe's version information), and where it will be installed. 2. What it needs: Linux (Debian) set up, Wine, or Android, each with the size of its download. The wizard sets them up itself, behind an administrator's password, with a progress bar (as Install Wine does today). 3. Installing: a progress bar from the job's own output, and the full log behind "Details".

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera › The wizard (all file types)
docs.t: 4. Done: "Open <app>", "Put it on the desktop", and where it is in the Start menu. A failure says why, in plain words, from the last lines of the log. Installing needs an administrator (or their password), as installing from the App Store does. Every installed app can be removed again from Settings › Apps.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera › Each file type
docs.t: .deb (Debian packages): rudolf-debian deb FILE copies the file into Debian and installs it with apt-get install, which fetches what it depends on. The app's launcher appears in the Start menu, with its own icon. Uninstall: apt-get remove, from Settings › Apps › Linux. .exe and .msi (Windows): the wizard runs the installer with Wine (wine or wine msiexec /i). It tells which programs appeared in the Start menu afterwards, and offers to put them on the desktop. A program that is not an installer, but the app itself, is offered "Keep it in Programs and add it to the Start menu" instead.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera › Each file type
docs.t: .AppImage: kept in a Programs folder of the account (~/Applications), made runnable, and given a Start-menu launcher with the icon from inside it (--appimage-extract of the .desktop file and the icon only). It runs in Debian, which has the libraries AppImages expect; one that needs FUSE runs with --appimage-extract-and-run. .bin (Linux installers): these are programs that install something else (drivers, games, tools); what they do differs for each one. The wizard shows what the file is (file), warns that it runs with the account's rights in Debian, and runs it in a Terminal window, where its own questions can be answered. Not as administrator.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera › Each file type
docs.t: .apk (Android apps): through Waydroid, which runs Android in a container. - the kernel needs Android's binder (CONFIG_ANDROID_BINDER_IPC, CONFIG_ANDROID_BINDERFS) and a few container options: a kernel change, checked in kconfig.sh like the others; - Waydroid itself comes from Debian; the Android system image (about 800 MB, LineageOS) is downloaded the first time, behind a confirmation; - Android apps show in a window of their own (Waydroid runs a small Wayland display inside X); - Google Play's apps that need Google services may not work; the wizard says so before the download.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera › Each file type
docs.t: .ipa (iPhone and iPad apps): these cannot be installed. iPhone apps are built for Apple's own system and are encrypted for Apple's devices; nothing outside Apple's devices can run them. The wizard says so, and offers to look for the same app in the App Store (Linux) or as a web app.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera › Fewer console apps (added 2026-11-09)
docs.t: Terminal takes in the Command Prompt: one app with the Command Prompt's icon, a tab for the Command Prompt (drive C:, everywhere) and tabs for Linux (Debian). It opens on Linux when Linux is set up; prompt() (Lua, .BAT, rpk) opens a C: tab. The Start menu has one Terminal; "Terminal (Linux)" and the Command Prompt entry go. The Developer Console leaves the Start menu unless Settings › Apps › "Show developer tools" is on; it stays in Task Manager and in search. The Code Editor stays: it is an editor, not a console.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Added on 2026-11-09: installing apps from files, and the camera › The camera
docs.t: The device (#136): cameras (video*, media*, v4l-subdev*) belong to the video group the desktop is in. Checked on the Vivobook after the fix: the Camera app (photos and video), Oracle's websites asking for the camera (the shell's permission prompt), Discord's video calls (Flatpak, which has the device), and Settings › Privacy › Camera off and on. Debian's programs (Wine included): /dev/video* placed in Debian like /dev/dri and /dev/snd. Cameras of other laptops: Intel's MIPI cameras (IPU6, 1.5.4's kernel options) need libcamera rather than UVC; only checked on hardware that has one. Hardware check (hwcheck30): the camera step opens it for a moment and says which camera it found.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 1. Where the files go
docs.t: ` /persist/accounts/<account id>/ one per account, encrypted with its file key (fscrypt v2, AES-256-XTS) Desktop/ Documents/ Pictures/ Music/ Videos/ Downloads/ .Trash/ the account's Trash (files, and where each came from) .rudolf/ the desktop's notes on files (comments, favourites, sort orders) /persist/accounts/guest/ tmpfs, emptied at sign-out (as the guest's home is today) ` C:\USERS\<name> is that folder. The other parts of C: (Programs, the system folders) stay in fs:system: they are small and the same for everyone. Names keep their case on the disk. The desktop's names are upper case today. The view shows a file as it is named, and compares names without case, so Report.pdf and REPORT.PDF are one file (a second one is Report (2).pdf).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 1. Where the files go
docs.t: While an account is signed in, /home/rudolf/Documents, Pictures, Downloads, Music, Videos and Games are bind mounts of that account's folders. Every Linux app (Flatpak, Debian, Wine, Steam) sees that account's files. Nothing is mounted while nobody is signed in.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 2. rudolfd: files in the homes
docs.t: A new file API (home/*), only inside /persist/accounts/<the signed-in account> (and an administrator's opened account): list, tree, stat: names, folder or file, size, modified time, a version number (mtime and size) for "changed elsewhere". read (with ranges, for viewers and the antivirus) and link (as /dlf/, for <video> and PDFs). write: whole file or appended chunks, then an atomic rename. It refuses a write whose base version is out of date (the file changed meanwhile), and the desktop asks which copy to keep. mkdir, rename, move, copy (a job when large), delete (into .Trash/), purge. watch: changes made by Linux apps (inotify), passed on as events, so File Explorer and open apps update.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 2. rudolfd: files in the homes
docs.t: Path checks: absolute paths built by rudolfd from the account and a relative path. No .., and no links leading out. Keys: POST home/unlock (the account's file key, sent once over the local API after the desktop unwraps it) adds the fscrypt key and mounts the binds. home/lock removes the key and unmounts them, at sign-out and at switch-user.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 3. The desktop: C: as a view
docs.t: The apps keep using the in-memory tree (node(), d[name]=value, fsSave()), so they need no changes: At sign-in, the home's tree is read from the disk (tree): names, sizes, times. A file's content is read when it is first opened. Small text files (under 256 KB) are read at once in the background, so search and previews do not wait. A file not read yet is a reference, as downloads are today, generalised from rudolfdisk: to every file. Opening it reads it. Viewers that already read references in pieces (video, PDF, images) keep doing so.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 3. The desktop: C: as a view
docs.t: Saving: - fsFlush() no longer writes the home as one record. It compares the tree with the last version written (strings are compared by identity first, which costs nothing when unchanged) and writes only files that changed, made or went away, through home/write, mkdir, rename and delete; - a crash or power cut loses at most the last 300 ms, as today, and never a whole home; - renames and moves inside C: are found from File Explorer's own operations (cut, paste, rename, drag), which call rudolfd directly rather than going through the comparison.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 3. The desktop: C: as a view
docs.t: Changes from outside (a Linux app saved a file): watch events update the tree. If the file is open and edited in the desktop, the app is told and asks: keep mine, or reload. The rest of C: (fs:system), the browser-only version and live sessions without RUDOLFDATA keep the current storage, unchanged.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 4. Moving the homes (once, at an account's first sign-in on 1.5.6)
docs.t: 1. The desktop decrypts the home record as today. 2. It writes every file to /persist/accounts/<id>/, which is already encrypted. Large downloads (the .accounts/<id>/ files) are moved, not copied. 3. It reads the tree back and compares names, sizes and SHA-256s with the record. 4. Only then does it switch to the disk. It keeps the old record for the update fallback: if 1.5.6 does not start twice in a row, the computer goes back to 1.5.5, which still has the old record. Files changed after the move would then show their old version in 1.5.5. The notification says so, and the record is deleted once 1.5.6 has been the working system for 7 days. Other cases:

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 4. Moving the homes (once, at an account's first sign-in on 1.5.6)
docs.t: A home that cannot be moved (a full disk, a damaged record) stays as it is, with a notification and a health-log line. Nothing is lost, and the move is tried again at the next sign-in. C:\SHARED DOWNLOADS (BEFORE 1.5.5) moves to /persist/accounts/shared-downloads/, readable by every account, if it is still there. Progress is shown, because a large home takes a while: "Moving your files to the disk… 1,234 of 5,678 files".

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 5. What changes with it
docs.t: Downloads: - Oracle's checked downloads move straight into the account's Downloads/; - the 1.5 MB split, the rudolfdisk: entries, the reconcile and the adoption (#115, #117) go away; - .incoming and .quarantine stay. "Encrypt my data": - Debian and Flatpak stay in /persist/vault; - Downloads leaves it, because it is now inside each account's own encrypted folder; - the setting says that homes are always encrypted, and that "Encrypt my data" covers Linux. The Trash is .Trash/ in the account's folder: restoring is a rename, and its size comes from the disk. 1.5.5's Trash items move with the home. Storage, search and duplicates (1.5.5 items 4, 6, 7) use rudolfd on the disk. Search can read every file.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 5. What changes with it
docs.t: Backup: - "Back up everything" makes one archive of every account's folder, read through the keys of the accounts that are signed in. Accounts that are not signed in are copied with their fscrypt-encrypted names and contents, which restore only onto this computer's RUDOLFDATA. The page says so, and offers a backup per account, decrypted, for another computer; - restoring older backups (records) goes through the move in item 4. Administrators opening an account's files (acct50) adds that account's key while the administrator has the folder open, and removes it when they close it. The guest: a tmpfs home, as now. Settings › Storage shows homes as real sizes on the disk.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 6. Risks, and how each is handled
docs.t: Losing files in the move: - it copies, verifies with SHA-256, and keeps the old record for 7 days; - QEMU tests move homes of 10 and 5,000 files, and one with a damaged record. An app that writes a file the desktop has open: versions on every write, and the app asks when they differ. Speed: opening a file is a local HTTP call to rudolfd (milliseconds). Listing a folder of 10,000 files is measured in the QEMU test and must stay under 1 s. fscrypt on older drives: the encrypt feature is added to RUDOLFDATA as "Encrypt my data" does today (tune2fs -O encrypt). A drive that cannot take it (not ext4) keeps today's storage, and says so.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 6. Risks, and how each is handled
docs.t: Two people's files in Linux apps: the bind mounts change at sign-in. An app left running from the previous account is stopped at switch-user, as Linux apps are today when the account changes. Going back to 1.5.5: covered for 7 days by the kept record (item 4). After that, a fallback to 1.5.5 would see an empty home. The update keeps 1.5.6 from falling back past 7 days, and says so.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 7. Tests
docs.t: Host: rudolfd's home/* against a temporary ext4 image with the encrypt feature (root): - paths that try to leave the folder; - versions and conflicts; - unlock and lock (the files unreadable after lock); - bind mounts. Browser (stand-in rudolfd with a disk in memory): - the view; - only changed files written; - references read on open; - outside changes; - the move with verification and a damaged record.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 7. Tests
docs.t: QEMU t156: - a 1.5.5 home with documents, pictures and a large download, updated to 1.5.6: files on the disk, encrypted after sign-out, readable after sign-in; - a Linux app (busybox in Debian) sees and edits a document, and the desktop shows the edit; - the fallback to 1.5.5 within the 7 days shows the old home; - a backup and its restore; - two accounts, an administrator opening the other's files. The Vivobook: your real home moved; Oracle, Steam, Emu, Notepad, WordPro, Paint and the Linux apps on the same files.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 8. The last change before release: one Start button
docs.t: Moved from the 1.5.7 plan (its Part 3, item 7) on 2026-11-10. This, and any fixes it needs, are the last changes before 1.5.6 is released.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 8. The last change before release: one Start button
docs.t: One button for the logo and the version (asked for on 2026-11-10, for 1.5.7; moved here the same day). The taskbar has the logo (Start) and, right beside it, "Rudolf OS 1.5.6" (#osver, misc25.js), which opens Settings › About: two buttons next to each other that both lead into the same place. They become one button: the logo with "Rudolf OS" and the version beside it, in one frame, that does only what the Start button does (a click opens the Start menu, a right-click its menu, and the keyboard and screen readers know it as "Start"). Settings › About stays where it is, in Settings and the Start menu. On a taskbar at the left or the right (150 px wide) the text goes under the logo, or is left out when it does not fit. The screen saver and About's picture take the logo from it as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 8. The last change before release: one Start button
docs.t: The whole version number, whatever it is (asked for on 2026-11-10): the text is the full version as the system has it (RVER, from the release's version), never a fixed "1.5" or a pattern of three one-digit parts. It must show 1.5.7, 1.10.0, 1.12.15, 2.0 and 10.3.1 whole; the button's width follows the text, and only the side taskbars may leave the text out, never cut it. Anything that compares versions (the update check, "what's new", the Library's minimum versions) compares them part by part as numbers (1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.9), and a test covers these versions.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › 8. The last change before release: one Start button
docs.t: Built in 1.5.6: misc25.js (the version is a part of the Start button, .stv; the second button is gone), styles25.css (beside the logo at the bottom and the top, under it at the left and the right, on two lines there if need be, never cut), core25.js verCmp (versions part by part as numbers; What's new lists them newest first with it; nothing else compares versions today: updates go by the release's serial, and the Library has no minimum versions yet). Test: iso/qt/shell2/startbtn56_t.js.

The move for existing homes, with verification and the kept record (browser tests, QEMU t156). 4. Downloads, the Trash, Linux apps' folders, "Encrypt my data", backup and restore on the new storage.

(added 2026-11-09) Installation wizards, one PR each: Debian sees the account's folders (#137) and the wizard with .deb; .exe and .msi; .AppImage and .bin; .apk (kernel binder, Waydroid); .ipa's explanation goes with the first. The camera: the device (#136), then Debian's /dev/video and the hardware check. 6. QEMU t150, t150f, t152 and t156 on the final beta; the Vivobook; then promote when you say; the disc image.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.6: your files on the disk › Size
docs.t: rudolfd (about 600 lines) and the desktop (a new storage layer of about 500 lines, and less in dl27.js and linux26.js). No new packages: fscrypt's ioctls are already used by rudolfd's vault (1.5.0).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught
docs.t: Asked for on 2026-11-09, after the Vivobook tests of the 1.5.6 betas. 1.5.6 finishes first (its installation wizards, the camera, the Terminal and 1.5.5's remaining File Explorer items); this plan starts once 1.5.6 is promoted. Four parts: 1. Blitzen diagnostics: Blitzen reads the computer's own state and Rudolf OS's documents, and explains what went wrong, without changing anything. 2. Recommended improvements: what the 1.5.6 betas showed on real hardware: a deleted download, a wrong path, a setting lost between requests, a browser restarted after sleep. Each led to a fix; these make the next ones less likely, and quicker to find.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught
docs.t: 3. Apps, games and start-up (added on 2026-11-09, after Steam and Among Us on the Vivobook): stopping apps, saying what the memory guard did, the network at start-up, and what 1.5.6 leaves for later. (Three more found that day went into 1.5.6 itself: prompts in front of full-screen games, installer windows hidden behind the desktop, and Chromium's own shortcuts that could close the desktop.) 4. WebKit for the desktop, Chromium only for browsing (added on 2026-11-10): the desktop and its built-in apps run in WebKit, a lighter web engine, so that they take much less of the memory; Chromium stays, as the web browser, started only to browse.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › What is there today (checked in the code and on the Vivobook)
docs.t: Blitzen (1.3.x, blitzen26.js) is the offline assistant: a small model run by llama.cpp (rudolf-ai, started on demand by rudolfd), with a context of 8,192 tokens by default. It answers about code (BlockLua, Lua, Luau, Pilot.lua, JavaScript, C++, Python) with context packs (blitzpacks26.js): short reference cards, each under about 800 words, sent with a question. "Ask Blitzen" is in Notepad, the Code Editor, BlockLua Builder and the Terminal. The Vivobook (the test computer): Ryzen 3 7320U, 3.4 GB of memory, about 1.2 GB used with the desktop open. A model that fits beside the desktop has about 1 to 3 billion parameters.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › What is there today (checked in the code and on the Vivobook)
docs.t: What the computer records about itself: - the health log (/persist/var/log/health.log, System health): start-ups, crashes, the browser restarted, sign-in failures, the encrypted folder; - rudolfd's log (/run/rudolf/rudolfd.log, lost at restart), session.log, the job log of the last task; - the system report (tm26.js sysReport, "Report a problem"): version, hardware, drivers, storage, network; - the hardware check (hwcheck30): keyboard, touchpad, camera, battery, screen; - the desktop's own events (logEvt, Event Viewer), which stay in the desktop's storage.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › What is there today (checked in the code and on the Vivobook)
docs.t: What could not be seen during the 1.5.6 tests: - the desktop's errors were to go to /run/rudolf/page.log (/api/clientlog), but no page.log was ever written on the Vivobook, also when the 1.5.6 Downloads clean-up should have reported; - rudolfd's log is gone after a restart.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 1: Blitzen diagnostics › What it does
docs.t: "Why?" next to what failed: - a notification of an error ("Your files could not be opened", an install that failed); - a line of the health log or the Event Viewer; - the installation wizard's failure, the Terminal's last command. "What's wrong with this computer?" in System health: Blitzen reads the latest problems and says, in plain words: - what happened and when; - the likely cause, with the log line it comes from; - what to do: a setting to change, something to install, or "report it" when it is a fault in Rudolf OS.

docs.t: "Draft a report": the problem, the steps, the system report and the relevant log lines in one text, for the person to read and send (Report a problem, or to the developers). Nothing is sent by Blitzen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 1: Blitzen diagnostics › What it reads (read-only)
docs.t: Rudolf OS's documents, as reference material found by search, not training: - the CHANGELOG (what changed in which version, and the known fixes); - the plans in docs/ (how each part works: the disk, Downloads, the wizards, encryption, updates); - the Help pages and the Settings search entries. Kept with the release as a small index (/usr/share/rudolf/blitzen-docs), split into sections of about 300 words, and searched by words (BM25) before each question. The best few sections go with the question: the model's context is small, so only what matters is sent.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 1: Blitzen diagnostics › What it reads (read-only)
docs.t: This computer's state, through a new rudolfd endpoint ai/facts that only reads: - the health log (last 100 lines), rudolfd's log, session.log (filtered: no passwords, tokens or keys), the last job's log; - the system report; - the desktop's events (sent by the desktop with the question); - the hardware check's last result. The person sees what is sent to the model ("Blitzen will read: …") and can remove lines first. It all stays on this computer, as Blitzen already does.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 1: Blitzen diagnostics › What it does not do
docs.t: No changes: Blitzen does not run commands, change settings, install, delete or move files. It suggests; the person does it (with a button to open the right page when there is one). Anthropic's terms do not allow training a general assistant on Claude's outputs without written permission, and this plan does not: the documents are searched, not trained on. No promises it cannot keep: answers say how sure they are, and quote the log line they rest on. When nothing in the logs explains a problem, it says so and offers the report.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 1: Blitzen diagnostics › Size and speed on the Vivobook
docs.t: The index of documents: about 2 MB, searched in the desktop in under 100 ms. An answer of a few sentences from a 1 to 3B model on 4 cores: about 10 to 30 seconds. The answer streams as it comes. When memory is short (a game, a large page), Blitzen says it will answer when there is room, as today.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 1: Blitzen diagnostics › Tests
docs.t: Host: ai/facts filters secrets (a test log with a token, a password line and a key) and reads only the files it lists. Browser (a stand-in model that echoes what it received): the right sections and log lines are sent for a known failure; nothing is sent without the person seeing it; no button runs a command. On the Vivobook: three real problems from the 1.5.6 betas (a download not found, a package not readable, sleep restarting the browser), asked as the person would ask. The answer must name the right cause or say it does not know.

docs.t: 5. Memory in System health (asked for on 2026-11-09). A Memory section in Settings › System health, beside Power and battery: - Compressed memory: Automatic (as large as the memory, at most 8 GiB, as since 1.5.6; recommended), Smaller (half of it, as before 1.5.6) or Off. No free size: too small runs out sooner, too large spends the computer's time compressing. A change applies at the next restart (shrinking a full one would stall the computer); the rudolf.nozram=1 start-up option stays, and wins. Kept in /persist/etc/rudolf-memory, read by /usr/lib/rudolf/memory, set through a rudolfd endpoint memory/settings (administrators). - Now: memory in use, and how much is compressed and how full it is (as Task Manager shows). - What the memory guard closed in the last 7 days, from the health log (on 2026-11-09 a Newgrounds Flash game's page at 1,882 MB; Discord, when it is closed as a background app), each with its time and size. - "Close apps with no window open when memory runs out", on by default (the memory guard's rule since 1.5.6).

docs.t: Asked for on 2026-11-10, after the comparison with Ubuntu and Mint: of the ways to make the desktop lighter, this one needs the least work for the largest gain.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 4: WebKit for the desktop, Chromium only for browsing › Why
docs.t: On the Vivobook (3.4 GB) the desktop's own Chromium takes about 780 MB (its main process, the desktop page, the graphics process, the network process), and more with web pages open. With Steam, Discord and a game, that is what ran out: the white screens and the watchdog's restarts of 1.5.6 (#160, #167) came from it. The desktop and every built-in app (File Explorer, the Office apps, Settings, the App Store, the emulators, Blitzen) are web code (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, WebAssembly). A native desktop (Xfce, LXQt, Qt or GTK) would mean writing them all again; another web engine runs them as they are.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 4: WebKit for the desktop, Chromium only for browsing › Why
docs.t: WebKit (WPE WebKit with its small launcher Cog, or WebKitGTK) is the engine of GNOME's Web and of many devices' screens; it usually takes noticeably less memory per page than Chromium. How much less on the Vivobook is measured first (step 1), before anything is changed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 4: WebKit for the desktop, Chromium only for browsing › What changes
docs.t: The desktop page (the desktop, the taskbar, the Start menu and every built-in app) runs in Cog (WPE WebKit), in place of the Chromium kiosk. The session starts it the same way, in the desktop's memory group (#160), with the same watchdog (its heartbeat is the same request to rudolfd). Web pages (Oracle Browser, the links in apps, sign-in pages, Newgrounds, cloud gaming) open in Chromium, as a separate window: started when someone browses, closed when its last window is. Today they open in tabs inside the desktop (the shell's Controlled Frames); they become Chromium's own windows and tabs, with Rudolf OS's policies (downloads into the account's Downloads, the camera prompt, the keyboard shortcuts of #151).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 4: WebKit for the desktop, Chromium only for browsing › What changes
docs.t: What only Chromium has, and what replaces it: - the shell (an Isolated Web App with Controlled Frames): not needed by the desktop any more; the web pages are Chromium's own windows (above); - the Ruffle extension (Flash in web pages): Flash Player (the built-in app) already plays SWF files with Ruffle's web build; in web pages, Chromium keeps the extension; - the frames extension (web pages inside the desktop's frames): not needed (the pages open in Chromium); - Chromium's policies and flags for the desktop (shortcuts, the camera, the GPU): WebKit's own settings, and the keyboard guard of #151 in the page itself; - the memory guard's "the largest web page": it closes Chromium's tabs, as now; the desktop itself is WebKit and is not one of them.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Part 4: WebKit for the desktop, Chromium only for browsing › What changes
docs.t: Kept as it is: rudolfd and everything it does, the accounts, the files, Linux apps (Flatpak), Debian and Wine, the updates. The desktop talks to rudolfd as it does today.

docs.t: System Settings › Desktop engine: a list, Standard (Chromium) or Lite (WebKit, test); the choice is kept in /persist/etc/rudolf-desktop-engine and taken by rudolf-init at start-up, so it applies at the next restart. Lite is rudolf-webkit (iso/sys/rudolf-webkit.c, WebKitGTK 4.1) in the system layer, with what it needs gathered by systools/addwebkit.sh from the release machine's Ubuntu 24.04 (its helper processes, GStreamer's basic plug-ins, GLib's TLS module): it starts before sign-in, with or without Debian and "Encrypt my data". (A first version used WebKitGTK in Debian, which with Debian in the encrypted folder, as on the Vivobook, could not start before sign-in.) Not yet: H.264 and AAC (GStreamer's libav plug-in, about 30 MB more). The workflow "Lite engine check" builds it and opens the desktop page in it on a virtual screen whenever its files change. docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.7: Blitzen diagnostics, and what the 1.5.6 tests taught › Added on 2026-11-10: safeguards against a computer that cannot start
docs.t: The Vivobook could not start the 1.5.7 beta with the Lite desktop engine, and Recovery mode, a boot-files-only rescue stick and a stick's updater each made it worse (the account is in docs/plan-1.5.8.md). Priorities 1 to 3 of the safeguards went into 1.5.7: a desktop that cannot start is given up (Lite on trial until it answers once), a system slot missing a layer goes back to the previous one, Recovery mode starts the installed system with safe settings, recovery and stick starts never update the installed system, and updates are self-contained and checked complete. Priorities 4 and 5 are docs/plan-1.5.8.md.

Every step below is done or moved to docs/plan-1.5.9.md ("Moved from 1.5.8"); the last additions were Make a stick's full rescue sticks (5.1), the dynamic backgrounds (Glacier Lake, Spirit Falls, their moving parts paused when unseen) and the fixes found on the Vivobook with beta 2026111214.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery
docs.t: Asked for on 2026-11-10, after the Vivobook could not start the 1.5.7 beta with the Lite desktop engine. The safeguards that stop such a failure from leaving a computer unable to start went into 1.5.7 (priorities 1 to 3 below); this plan is the rest (priorities 4 and 5). It starts once 1.5.7 is promoted. Added the same day: mobile data (Part 6, after looking at a Verizon MiFi 7730L), Android apps (Part 7: the .apk work delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds) and mobile form factors (Part 8: x86 handhelds and tablets first, then a lean phone-capable Rudolf OS over the next versions) and Oracle's tabs in WebKit (Part 9: a real browser in the Lite desktop).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › What happened (2026-11-10)
docs.t: 1. Lite (WebKit) was chosen for the desktop. On the Vivobook's graphics it closed as it started, every 7 to 9 seconds; the session started it again without end, because its safety net only caught a desktop that hangs. The screen stayed grey and the computer never reached the sign-in screen. Lite had been tried on Xvfb and in Debian's own WebKit (cog), never on the Vivobook's real graphics.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › What happened (2026-11-10)
docs.t: 2. Recovery mode skipped the installed system for the drive's own, and an installed computer's drive has boot files only: "this drive has boot files only (1.2.8)". The rescue stick at hand had boot files only too, and both drives showed the same message, so it took three tries to see which drive had started. Fast Boot also skipped the stick until it was chosen in the ASUS boot menu.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › What happened (2026-11-10)
docs.t: 3. A full 1.5.6 stick (written with Rufus in DD mode from the Asus desktop) got through. Started in Recovery mode, it ran the stick's 1.5.6 with the Vivobook's 1.5.7 files: the desktop asked for the shell again and again and kept restarting. Its updater then put 1.5.7 in the spare slot taking the Chromium layer from the stick, and scheduled it; without the stick that slot could not start, and the start-up stopped at the same boot-files-only message (it went back to the good system at the following start only because the slot's tries had run out). chip then did not answer at start-up ("Codec #0 probe error", after the forced power-offs); a full shut-down fixed it. in /run, lost at each restart.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Done in 1.5.7 (priorities 1 to 3)
docs.t: A desktop that cannot start is given up (session: desk_exited, webkit_trial_*, shell_switch_limit; test qt/host/deskfall57_t.sh): Lite closing 3 times in a row as it starts, or not having answered before the computer was switched off, is turned off for good (Settings says when and why); the shell likewise until the next start; a desktop asking for the shell more than 3 times in 5 minutes is not obeyed. A system that cannot be put together goes back to the previous one (initramfs: a slot missing a layer is given up like a damaged one; test qt/host/startfall57_t.sh).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Done in 1.5.7 (priorities 1 to 3)
docs.t: Recovery mode starts the installed system with safe settings and changes nothing (initramfs; the session already leaves out Lite, the shell and the graphics driver in recovery). Needs 1.5.7 boot files. Recovery and stick starts never change the installed system (rudolf-update: no download in recovery, or from a disc that is not on RUDOLFDATA's drive; boot-ok does nothing in recovery; Settings says why; tests qt/host/updsafe57_t.sh and qt/shell2/updsafe57_t.js). Updates are self-contained and checked complete (rudolf-update: a layer shared with a removable disc is copied into the slot; a slot is only scheduled when every file is there at its listed size).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Priority 4: diagnosing a computer whose desktop does not start › 4.1 Start logs that outlast a restart
docs.t: Keep the session log, Lite's log (webkit-desktop.log), the start-up's choice of system (which slot, why, recovery or not) and the kernel's warnings of the last 4 starts in /persist/var/log/starts/ (rotated like rudolfd.log), written as they happen, not at shut-down. The initramfs writes its decisions (slot chosen, tries left, layer missing, slot given up) to RUDOLFDATA before kexec, so a start that never reaches rudolf-init still leaves a record. System health shows "Last starts" with the outcome of each; the self-test and Blitzen's diagnostics read them.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Priority 4: diagnosing a computer whose desktop does not start › 4.2 The devlink and remote access without the desktop
docs.t: starts it at boot when its time is left, and whether it waits for the desktop or the network the desktop sets up). independent of the desktop process, once the network is up. Remote access serves the X screen, so it shows a grey or broken desktop too: make sure it does not depend on the desktop page either.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Priority 4: diagnosing a computer whose desktop does not start › 4.3 Emergency keys in rudolf-display
docs.t: A key combination handled by rudolf-display itself (which reads the keyboard before X, as Ctrl+Alt+Del does) that switches the desktop back to the standard engine at once and restarts it: for example Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12, with an on-screen line from rudolf-display saying it did. The same keys in Recovery mode do nothing (already safe).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Priority 5: smoother recovery and fewer surprises › 5.1 Rescue media that say what they are
docs.t: Make a stick writes a full rescue system by default; a boot-files-only stick stays possible but says so on its boot menu title and when it starts. Start-up messages name the drive they are about ("the USB stick SanDisk 64 GB" / "this computer's drive") and say what to do next. The "boot files only (1.2.8)" message drops the version (it is when the feature came, not the drive's version) and says whether a rescue stick was found.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Priority 5: smoother recovery and fewer surprises › 5.2 Help: starting from a stick
docs.t: A Help page: Fast Boot (ASUS and others) can skip USB sticks; use the one-time boot menu (Esc or F8 on ASUS, F12 on many others) or turn Fast Boot off; write sticks in DD mode; Windows then calls the stick "not accessible" (do not format it); choose Recovery mode in Rudolf OS's menu.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Priority 5: smoother recovery and fewer surprises › 5.3 A speaker chip that does not answer
docs.t: The self-test checks that every sound card's codec answered at start-up (the kernel's "no codecs initialized" / "Codec #N probe error"), and System health says "The sound chip did not answer at start-up: shut down fully (not restart), wait 10 seconds and turn the computer on". rudolf-init tries once to reset it (unbind and bind the HD Audio device) before the desktop starts.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Priority 5: smoother recovery and fewer surprises › 5.4 Test where the risk is
docs.t: A rule for the repository: anything that changes how the desktop starts (engine, shell, display) has its fallback tested first, on the real graphics path (Xorg with the GPU, in QEMU with virtio-gpu and on the Vivobook), not only on the software display; it reaches the Vivobook only after that. libGLESv2.so.2": WebKit opens it while running, so addwebkit.sh's ldd pass never saw it. Fixed in 1.5.7 (addwebkit.sh copies it; the self-test checks it; webkit-check.yml runs Lite from the base layer in a chroot). With it, Lite ran, but GTK could not use the GPU ("No available configurations for the given pixel format", Xorg with modesetting on AMD): WebKit draws in software. Left for 1.5.8: GPU drawing for Lite (GTK's GL on this X server), and its effect on memory and speed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Priority 5: smoother recovery and fewer surprises › 5.4 Test where the risk is
docs.t: Found on 2026-11-11 (the release's base layer in a chroot, Xvfb with GLX, no GPU needed): the message is GTK 3's GLX check, and WebKit then turns acceleration off ("Disabled hardware acceleration because GTK failed to initialize GL"). The base layer had GLVND's libGLX.so.0 but no Mesa GLX driver (libGLX_mesa.so.0, which needs libxcb-glx.so.0). With both, the warning is gone and WebKit keeps acceleration on. addwebkit.sh copies them, the self-test checks them (lite-gpu), webkit-check.yml fails on the warning. Left: on the Vivobook, memory and speed with the GPU against software (Lite's point is memory), and a driver that hangs; if it costs too much, a setting.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Staging toward 1.6.0, the first cellular release (added on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: Parts 6 to 8 are staged across three versions (docs/plan-1.5.9.md, docs/plan-1.6.0.md): 1.5.8 (this plan): Oracle's tabs in WebKit (Part 9); the network groundwork: 6.1 the kernel's USB modem drivers, 6.2 adapters plugged in after start-up, 6.3 metered connections; 7.1 the .apk wizard's information, 7.2 scrcpy, the kernel side of 7.3 (binder); 8.1 begun (the tablet layout in the desktop, with browser tests). 1.5.9: ModemManager (read only), the WWAN kernel subsystem and the operators' database; 8.1 finished (tablet mode, on-screen keyboard, rotation); 8.2 the ARM64 build with QEMU checks on a test channel; 6.4 Share this connection; 7.3 Waydroid in Debian; the first phone prepared.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Staging toward 1.6.0, the first cellular release (added on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: 1.6.0: cellular: SIM and PIN, APNs, connecting, priorities and failover, data limits, signal and status, SMS (Messages), airplane mode, the FCC unlock for laptop modules; the first ARM64 release. Voice and emergency calls, and phones themselves, in 1.6.x (8.3). 6.5 (a hotspot's own status) stays as written: Rudolf OS shows the connection, never signs in to the hotspot.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 6: mobile data (added on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: Looked at on 2026-11-10: a used Verizon Jetpack MiFi 7730L (Novatel/Inseego, January 2017) plugged into the Asus desktop. LTE Category 9 (3-carrier aggregation, 2x2 MIMO, nano SIM), Wi-Fi 802.11ac on 2.4 and 5 GHz at once (15 devices), a 4,400 mAh battery, a 2.4" 320x240 touchscreen, USB-C and USB-A, a Qualcomm modem (the chip is not published), and 128 MB of memory with 256 MB of storage. Rudolf OS cannot run on it: far too little memory and storage, and its firmware is signed and locked (no open firmware such as OpenWrt supports it). Its use is as the **cellular link of a Rudolf OS laptop or tablet**, over USB or Wi-Fi. On the Asus, Windows listed it as a device but not as a network adapter (USB tethering off in its menu, or no active SIM), so which USB protocol it uses is still to be seen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 6: mobile data (added on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: What Rudolf OS lacks for that (checked in the code on 2026-11-10):

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 6: mobile data (added on 2026-11-10) › 6.1 USB modems and tethered phones
docs.t: The kernel has the USB CDC Ethernet driver (USB_NET_CDCETHER) only. Add USB_NET_RNDIS_HOST (many hotspots and Android phones' USB tethering), USB_NET_CDC_NCM and USB_NET_CDC_MBIM (newer hotspots and phones), USB_NET_QMI_WWAN and USB_SERIAL_OPTION (cellular modules inside laptops and USB sticks), checked in kconfig.sh like the others. ModemManager (with libqmi and libmbim) for cellular modules that need to be told to connect, with the SIM's PIN asked by the desktop: 1.5.9 (read only) and 1.6.0 (connecting); hotspots and tethered phones need none of it (they hand out an address themselves), so 1.5.8 covers them fully.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 6: mobile data (added on 2026-11-10) › 6.2 A network adapter plugged in after start-up
docs.t: rudolf-init asks for an address (udhcpc) only on cables present at start-up. An adapter that appears later (a hotspot's USB cable, a phone's tethering switched on, a USB Ethernet dongle) gets none: mdev runs the same DHCP start for a new network interface, and stops it when it goes. Settings › Network lists it ("USB modem: MiFi 7730L").

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 6: mobile data (added on 2026-11-10) › 6.3 Metered connections
docs.t: A connection can be metered (cellular data with a cap): set automatically for USB modems and tethered phones and for Wi-Fi networks that say so (Android's hotspots set the ANDROID_METERED option in DHCP), and by hand in Settings › Network for any network. On a metered connection: no automatic system updates (sysupd25's daily check downloads nothing; Settings says why and offers it by hand), no automatic Library, Flathub or Blitzen downloads, no app store catalog refresh in the background; the browser and apps work as usual. rudolfd keeps the state (net/metered), the desktop reads it. Data used on each metered connection this month (from the interface's counters), in Settings › Network.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 6: mobile data (added on 2026-11-10) › 6.4 Rudolf OS as the hotspot ("Share this connection") (1.5.9)
docs.t: The Vivobook's Wi-Fi chip (rtw88 8821CE) supports access-point mode. Settings › Network › Share this connection: shares the connection Rudolf OS has (cable, USB modem, or Wi-Fi on a second adapter) over Wi-Fi with its own network name and password (hostapd, dnsmasq, and the firewall's NAT rules), off by default, administrators only. With one Wi-Fi chip, sharing a Wi-Fi connection over the same chip depends on the chip (concurrent station and access point): checked on the Vivobook first, otherwise offered only for cable and USB connections.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 6: mobile data (added on 2026-11-10) › 6.5 Battery and signal of a hotspot
docs.t: Hotspots and phones expose little over USB: what Rudolf OS can show without signing in to the hotspot is the connection itself (speed, data used). A hotspot's own admin page stays the hotspot's (its address in Settings › Network, opened in Oracle); Rudolf OS does not sign in to it or keep its password.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 7: Android apps (.apk), delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds (added on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: On 2026-11-10 .apk was moved out of 1.5.7: Waydroid needs the kernel's binder, Waydroid and its container tools in the system layer, and a first download of about 1 GB (the Android system image), which weighs on a 3.4 GB computer while the desktop is being made lighter. These are the ways to it, cheapest first; the .apk wizard (install56) offers what this computer can do.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 7: Android apps (.apk), delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds (added on 2026-11-10) › 7.1 Always: say what the .apk is, and offer what already works
docs.t: Opening an .apk shows the app's name, icon, version and the permissions it asks for (read from the file with aapt2 dump badging, from Debian's Android tools, or a small reader of the APK's manifest in rudolfd), never running it. It offers what Rudolf OS already runs: the app's web version (many Android apps are also websites or web apps; Oracle can keep one as an app in the Start menu) and the same app for Linux (Flathub, by name, in the App Store), when there is one.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 7: Android apps (.apk), delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds (added on 2026-11-10) › 7.2 The phone's own apps on Rudolf OS (scrcpy)
docs.t: An Android phone plugged in by USB (or on the same Wi-Fi) shows its screen in a Rudolf OS window and is used with the mouse and keyboard (with its sound on Android 11 or later): scrcpy (from Debian), over ADB. The apps run on the phone, so nothing is installed on the computer and nothing is downloaded beyond scrcpy (a few MB). It needs "USB debugging" turned on in the phone's developer options, by the phone's owner: Rudolf OS explains how and never changes anything on the phone itself. (Normal ADB only: not the diagnostic or download modes of a phone's chip, which can damage it.)

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 7: Android apps (.apk), delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds (added on 2026-11-10) › 7.2 The phone's own apps on Rudolf OS (scrcpy)
docs.t: scrcpy works with Android 5 or later; the phones seen on the Asus (a REDMAGIC 9 Pro, a moto g play) are recent enough.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 7: Android apps (.apk), delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds (added on 2026-11-10) › 7.3 Android apps on the computer (Waydroid), for computers with room for it
docs.t: The kernel side costs almost nothing and can ship first, in 1.5.8: ANDROID_BINDER_IPC, ANDROID_BINDERFS (and ANDROID_BINDER_DEVICES=""), with the namespaces and cgroups Waydroid's LXC container uses (most are on already), checked in kconfig.sh. Then Waydroid can be added later without a new kernel. Waydroid itself in Debian (already a download on demand), not in the system layer: apt install waydroid in Debian's container, with binderfs mounted into it, so the system layer does not grow and computers that never open an .apk pay nothing.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 7: Android apps (.apk), delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds (added on 2026-11-10) › 7.3 Android apps on the computer (Waydroid), for computers with room for it
docs.t: The Android image (LineageOS, about 800 MB) only when the person asks, behind a confirmation with the size, kept in the encrypted folder's storage like Debian, and removable in Storage. Offered only on computers with at least 4 GB of memory, or with the Lite desktop engine on (it frees roughly 300 to 500 MB), and the memory guard treats Waydroid's container as an app it may close. Each Android app gets its own window (Waydroid's multi-window mode, its Wayland display shown inside X with a small compositor), and a Start menu entry.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 7: Android apps (.apk), delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds (added on 2026-11-10) › 7.3 Android apps on the computer (Waydroid), for computers with room for it
docs.t: Apps that need Google's services (most from Google Play) may not work; the wizard says so before the download. Waydroid with OpenGApps or microG is left to the person (a setting in Waydroid, not something Rudolf OS installs).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 7: Android apps (.apk), delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds (added on 2026-11-10) › 7.4 Lighter, experimental: Android Translation Layer
docs.t: The Android Translation Layer (used by postmarketOS) runs some simple Android apps as ordinary Linux programs, with no Android image at all. It runs few apps today; looked at again once 7.3 works, as a light option for the apps it runs.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 7: Android apps (.apk), delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds (added on 2026-11-10) › 7.5 Rudolf OS on a phone
docs.t: The desktop's browser build (iso/www/index.html) already runs in any web browser, without rudolfd. On a phone it could be added to the home screen as a web app (a manifest and a service worker, so it opens offline and full screen), with the touch layout the desktop has for tablets: Notepad, WordPro, the games, Blitzen's packs and the files kept in the browser. Rudolf OS as a system on phone hardware (its own kernel on a phone) is not planned: phones' boot loaders are locked and their drivers closed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 7: Android apps (.apk), delayed from 1.5.7, with workarounds (added on 2026-11-10) › 7.6 iPhone apps (.ipa)
docs.t: Unchanged from 1.5.6's plan: they cannot run outside Apple's devices; the wizard says so and looks for a web or Linux version.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: The aim: Rudolf OS on handhelds, tablets and, within the next few versions, phones, while staying lean (a phone has 4 to 8 GB of memory and runs on a battery). Two routes, the cheap one first.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › What stands in the way today (checked in the code on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: x86 only: the release builds x86-64 layers, and x86 paths are written into ci_release.sh, addwebkit.sh, addnvk.sh and the self-test (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu). Phones are ARM64. One kernel for every PC, started by UEFI (systemd-boot, a signed UKI, Secure Boot). Phones need a kernel and a device tree per model, started by the phone's own boot loader (Android boot images, or U-Boot on the PinePhone Pro). A desktop for a mouse and keyboard: touch works (rudolf-display reads touchscreens), but there is no on-screen keyboard, no portrait layout, no gestures, and windows are sized for a large screen. No phone services: no cellular modem handling, calls or SMS, no suspend that keeps the modem listening, no screen rotation from the sensors, no phone cameras.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › What stands in the way today (checked in the code on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: Weight: the Chromium layer (about 130 MB compressed) and the standard engine's memory (about 830 MB on the Vivobook); Debian, Wine and Steam are already downloads on demand.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › Leanness rules for every mobile step
docs.t: 1. Lite (WebKit) is the desktop engine on mobile devices, not Standard: about a third of Chromium's memory (the 1.5.7 trial). Chromium becomes a download on demand there, for websites that need it. 2. Nothing heavy in the system layer: Debian, Wine, Steam, Waydroid, Blitzen's model, scrcpy and the like stay downloads on demand, behind a confirmation with the size, removable in Storage.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › Leanness rules for every mobile step
docs.t: 3. Measured on the device, against budgets: the system layers under 400 MB compressed; the desktop at the sign-in screen under 400 MB of memory with Lite (about 520 MB in the release check on 2026-11-10: WebKit's web process 389 MB, its UI 94 MB, its network process 35 MB, on Xvfb; reducing it is part of 8.2); idle power measured over an hour with the screen off. A release that breaks a budget says so in the release check, like the Lite engine check. 4. The same release, one system per architecture: one version number and one CHANGELOG; the desktop (the web page) is identical everywhere; only the layers below it differ.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › 8.1 x86 handhelds and tablets (1.5.8 to 1.5.9): no port needed
docs.t: Target devices: Steam Deck, ASUS ROG Ally, Lenovo Legion Go, Microsoft Surface Go and other x86 tablets. They start Rudolf OS as it is (UEFI, x86-64); Secure Boot as on any PC. Touch layout (the desktop): a tablet mode chosen automatically when there is a touchscreen and no keyboard (and by hand in Settings › Display): bigger targets, the taskbar as a dock, windows full screen one at a time, swipe from the bottom for the Start menu and from the right for notifications, portrait and landscape.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › 8.1 x86 handhelds and tablets (1.5.8 to 1.5.9): no port needed
docs.t: On-screen keyboard: part of the desktop page (it is a web page, so its own keyboard works in every built-in app and in Oracle's pages); for X programs (Linux and Windows apps), rudolf-display types its keys through XTest as it types the hardware keyboard's. Rotation from the accelerometer (iio-sensor-proxy, or reading /sys/bus/iio directly) through rudolf-display, which already rotates and scales the screen. Mobile data (Part 6) and battery care (1.4.4 on) apply as they are. Tests: browser tests at tablet and phone sizes (portrait 1080x2340 scaled, touch events); QEMU x86 with a touchscreen (-device virtio-tablet / usb-tablet with multitouch) and a portrait screen; then the Vivobook with the

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › 8.2 The ARM64 build (built and checked in QEMU in 1.5.9; first released in 1.6.0): Rudolf OS on ARM
docs.t: Build: the release workflow builds a second set of layers on GitHub's ARM64 runners (ubuntu-24.04-arm): the base layer, Lite (WebKitGTK for arm64), rudolfd and the C helpers (they are portable C), and the desktop page unchanged. The x86 paths become $(gcc -print-multiarch); addwebkit.sh and the self-test take the architecture from the system. Not on ARM64 at first: Steam and Windows programs (x86 only; Box64 or FEX as a later download, measured first), the NVIDIA (nvk) layer, Flash's Ruffle stays (it is WebAssembly). Updates: the same signed manifest format, with a list per architecture (beta/arm64/manifest.txt); the updater takes its architecture's list and never another's.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › 8.2 The ARM64 build (built and checked in QEMU in 1.5.9; first released in 1.6.0): Rudolf OS on ARM
docs.t: QEMU checks (what QEMU can confirm): qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt with UEFI (edk2), virtio-gpu, a virtio touchscreen, 3 to 4 GB of memory and a portrait screen: the system starts, the desktop runs in Lite, updates and rollback work, Recovery mode and the safeguards work, and a USB modem passed through to the virtual machine (the MiFi 7730L) gets an address. What QEMU cannot confirm: a phone's display, GPU, modem, cameras, sensors and audio drivers, its sleep and wake, battery life and heat, and how its boot loader starts the kernel. Those need the phone.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › 8.2 The ARM64 build (built and checked in QEMU in 1.5.9; first released in 1.6.0): Rudolf OS on ARM
docs.t: Generic ARM64 computers first: ARM64 laptops and boards that start with UEFI (Snapdragon X laptops as their mainline support matures; the Raspberry Pi 5 with its UEFI firmware) run the same image as QEMU.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › 8.3 Phones (1.6.x): one well-supported phone first
docs.t: Candidates (boot loader unlockable, good mainline Linux support; checked against the postmarketOS device list when the work starts): PinePhone Pro (made for Linux; the easiest to work on, slow), OnePlus 6/6T (Snapdragon 845, long among the best-supported Android phones on mainline Linux; cheap used), **Google Pixel 3a or a newer Pixel bought unlocked from Google (not one sold by Verizon), Fairphone 4/5** (the maker supports unlocking and Linux ports), Purism Librem 5 (Linux-first, expensive). The test phones at hand are not suitable: the moto g play XT2093DL is a carrier prepaid model, normally not unlockable; whether the REDMAGIC 9 Pro's boot loader unlocks is to be checked before relying on it. Only a phone that may be experimented on.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › 8.3 Phones (1.6.x): one well-supported phone first
docs.t: Per-phone kernel, shared everything else: a device package per phone (its kernel config fragment, device tree, firmware list, boot image format), built from postmarketOS's mainline work where it exists (their kernel configs and patches are the reference); the base, Lite and desktop layers are the ARM64 build's.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 8: mobile form factors, and a phone-capable Rudolf OS (added on 2026-11-10) › 8.3 Phones (1.6.x): one well-supported phone first
docs.t: Starting and updating: the phone's boot loader starts a Rudolf OS boot image (kernel, device tree, the same initramfs) from the boot partition; the A/B system slots, the signed manifest, rollback and the safeguards are the same as on a PC, kept on the userdata partition as RUDOLFDATA. Installing: from a computer, with fastboot (a guided page in Rudolf OS on the PC, and the steps in Help); the phone's boot loader stays unlocked, so it has no Secure Boot: the dm-verity check of each layer against the signed list still runs, and Settings says plainly that the phone's boot loader is unlocked.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 9: Oracle's tabs in WebKit (added on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: On the Vivobook with Lite (beta 2026111100, 2026-11-10), Oracle sent every website to Chromium's own window (the design of 1.5.7's Lite: the desktop page cannot show most sites in its frames, which sites forbid), and that window went behind the desktop at once, so browsing looked broken. With Standard, Oracle's tabs are real Chromium pages (the shell). Lite gets the same: Oracle's tabs as real WebKit pages.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 9: Oracle's tabs in WebKit (added on 2026-11-10) › 9.1 How
docs.t: rudolf-webkit (WebKitGTK, our own program) makes a web view per Oracle tab, laid over the desktop page exactly where Oracle draws its page area (a GtkOverlay above the desktop's view), shown, hidden, moved and closed as the page asks. A native view is not a frame: sites' frame protections do not apply, and sign-ins work as in a browser. The page and rudolf-webkit talk through a WebKit script message handler (page to program: open, navigate, back, forward, reload, stop, close, show, hide, place, zoom, find) and a script run in the page (program to page: address, title, icon, loading progress, security state, can-go-back, new tab or window wanted, download started).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 9: Oracle's tabs in WebKit (added on 2026-11-10) › 9.1 How
docs.t: Websites' data apart from the desktop's: their own WebKitWebsiteDataManager in ~/.rudolf-webkit/web, with cookies kept; private tabs with an ephemeral one; Settings › Oracle's clear-data buttons act on it. Popups and sign-in windows become new tabs (or a small window for window.open with a size, as sign-in popups need, with window.opener working so the sign-in returns to the page). Downloads through WebKitDownload into Downloads, shown in Oracle's downloads and the notifications, as dl27 does for Chromium's. Permissions (camera, microphone, location, notifications) asked through the desktop's own prompt, per site, remembered as Oracle's site settings. Fullscreen video: the tab's view fills the screen; Esc leaves.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 9: Oracle's tabs in WebKit (added on 2026-11-10) › 9.1 How
docs.t: Keyboard and focus: the tab's view has the focus when clicked; the desktop's shortcuts still work (rudolf-display and the program pass them to the page). Flash: Ruffle injected as a user script in the tabs (it is JavaScript and WebAssembly). Input from other windows: Task Manager, notifications and menus drawn by the desktop page stay above the tab views (the program hides or clips a view under them, as the shell does).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 9: Oracle's tabs in WebKit (added on 2026-11-10) › 9.2 What stays Chromium's
docs.t: Sites that need Widevine (Netflix, Spotify, Disney+), H.264/AAC where no other format is offered, Chrome-only sites and Chrome extensions: Oracle offers "Open in Chromium" (a button in the address bar and in the page's menu), and opens such sites there by itself when a site is on the list or a playback fails for want of a codec; the browser window comes to the front and stays there (the 1.5.7 bug fixed first, below). YouTube plays in WebKit through its VP9/AV1 and Opus streams.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 9: Oracle's tabs in WebKit (added on 2026-11-10) › 9.3 Leanness
docs.t: Each tab is a WebKit web process (about the size of a Chromium tab), with no second browser running at all unless a site needs Chromium; hidden tabs can be suspended (WebKit's page freezing), and the memory guard treats tab views as pages it may end, as it does Chromium's. No new layer: WebKitGTK is already in the system (1.5.7).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 9: Oracle's tabs in WebKit (added on 2026-11-10) › 9.6 FedCM on or off, in Oracle's ☰ menu (added on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: On the Vivobook, "Sign in with Google" on claude.ai went through Chromium's FedCM and stopped on a blank accounts.google.com/gsi/transform window; Firefox, without FedCM, signed in. 1.5.7 turns FedCM off in Chromium for everyone (PR #198). It is a choice, since some sites may come to need FedCM and Google may change its sign-in again: Oracle's ☰ menu: "Sign-in with FedCM" with a tick (off by default), and the same switch in Settings › Oracle › Sign-in, with one line on what it does ("Sites' 'Sign in with Google' buttons use Chromium's own sign-in. Turn it on only if a site asks for it; with it, Google's sign-in stopped on a blank window on some computers").

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 9: Oracle's tabs in WebKit (added on 2026-11-10) › 9.6 FedCM on or off, in Oracle's ☰ menu (added on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: Where it is kept: a system setting, /persist/etc/rudolf-browser.conf (fedcm=0|1), since Chromium's flags are set for the whole browser, not per account; rudolfd GET/POST web/fedcm (any signed-in account may change it, as other browser settings; guests cannot). The desktop page reads it at start-up for the menu's tick. What it changes: rudolfd web/open leaves FedCm out of --disable-features when on; the session reads the file when it starts the desktop's Chromium (Oracle's real tabs with Standard).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.8: diagnosing a computer that does not start, and smoother recovery › Part 9: Oracle's tabs in WebKit (added on 2026-11-10) › 9.6 FedCM on or off, in Oracle's ☰ menu (added on 2026-11-10)
docs.t: When it applies: the browser window is restarted at once if it is open (after asking: "Close the browser window to apply? Its tabs come back"; Chromium restores them); real tabs need the desktop's Chromium restarted, so the menu says "Applies to Oracle's tabs at the next sign-in or restart" and offers "Restart Oracle's tabs now" (the shell's restart, which keeps the session). Lite's WebKit tabs (9.1): WebKitGTK has no FedCM; the menu item is shown greyed with "Not used by WebKit tabs" while the tab is a WebKit one, and still applies to sites sent to Chromium (9.2).

docs.t: Done (2026-11-13), up to the device check: /usr/lib/rudolf/modem (start on mdev's cdc-wdm/wwan/ttyUSB of a modem driver, stop when the last goes; status from mmcli), the system bus shared with Bluetooth, rudolfd mobile/status, Settings › Network › Cellular modems; kconfig.sh's WWAN (MHI_WWAN_CTRL, MHI_WWAN_MBIM, IOSM, checked); ci_release.sh copies ModemManager, mmcli, qmi-proxy, mbim-proxy, the plug-ins and serviceproviders.xml with their libraries, and fails over 10 MB. Then (same day, without the device): ModemManager runs without udev, as on OpenWrt: started with --test-no-udev (--no-auto-scan on an older one), it applies its own udev rules (now in the base layer; the build fails without 80-mm-candidate.rules), and the modem service tells it of each port with mmcli --report-kernel-event: those already there when it starts (the network interfaces too, which mdev does not report), then each one mdev adds or removes. Udev-built with no udevd, it would have found no port marked ID_MM_CANDIDATE and seen no modem. To check on the Vivobook: the stick shows in Settings › Network › Cellular modems; /run/rudolf/modem.log has no "Invalid rule match" (ModemManager 1.22.0's u-blox rules broke its own rule reading, ModemManager issue 779).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.9: the groundwork for cellular (1.6.0) and for mobile devices › Part 8: developers, custom builds, and the official recovery (added on 2026-11-11) › 8.1 Three keys, not one
docs.t: The computer's key (device key): made in the computer's TPM 2.0 when it has one, never leaving it. It protects "Encrypt my data" (sealed to the TPM, so the disk opens only on this computer with its own start-up) and says "this computer". Without a TPM: a key protected by the account's password (as Encrypt my data is now). Lost with the hardware, by design. The publisher key (per person): Ed25519, signs a person's games or builds. Not tied to one computer: kept on a hardware security key (FIDO2/PIV: YubiKey and similar) or as a passphrase-protected file with an offline backup, as the Rudolf OS keys are. Losing a computer must not lose the right to update one's own games.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.9: the groundwork for cellular (1.6.0) and for mobile devices › Part 8: developers, custom builds, and the official recovery (added on 2026-11-11) › 8.1 Three keys, not one
docs.t: The account: links a person to their publisher key. Rudolf OS has no server of its own; the account is the person's GitHub account plus their publisher key registered in the Library (8.2). Settings › Accounts › Developer: makes or imports the publisher key, shows its public half and fingerprint, exports a backup, and (with a hardware

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.9: the groundwork for cellular (1.6.0) and for mobile devices › Part 8: developers, custom builds, and the official recovery (added on 2026-11-11) › 8.1 Three keys, not one
docs.t: Done (2026-11-13), the publisher key: User Settings › Developer makes one (WebCrypto Ed25519), keeps its private half only in a backup in Documents (PBKDF2-SHA-256 600 000 rounds, AES-GCM, a passphrase of 12 characters or more), the public half and fingerprint for the account; "Use a backup" brings it back; the private half is shown (60 s, after the passphrase) only to paste into a GitHub secret; its raw form is rpk-tool's. Not yet: hardware keys (FIDO2/PIV) and the computer's own key (TPM), which need the hardware to test. The three are separate so that a leaked signing key does not open anyone's files, and a broken laptop does not lock a developer out of their games.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.9: the groundwork for cellular (1.6.0) and for mobile devices › Part 8: developers, custom builds, and the official recovery (added on 2026-11-11) › 8.2 Publishing to the Library: a chain of trust
docs.t: approved developer: name, GitHub account, public key, what they may publish (package names under a prefix of their own), dates. Published as dev/<name>.cert in the Library. Packages carry their developer's signature and certificate; rpk accepts a package whose signature leads to the Library key through a valid certificate, and whose name the certificate allows. Revocation: a signed revoked.txt in the Library (keys and packages); rpk checks it with the index, and a revoked package is disabled on every computer at the next check (the App Store says why).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.9: the groundwork for cellular (1.6.0) and for mobile devices › Part 8: developers, custom builds, and the official recovery (added on 2026-11-11) › 8.2 Publishing to the Library: a chain of trust
docs.t: Done (2026-11-13): rpk-tool cert (the Library signs rpk-cert 1: name, github, key, prefix, expires) and build --cert (the package carries it: RPKSIG02 trailer); rpk accepts it like a Library package (desktop files only), under the prefix, never replacing someone else's, with a certificate from a trusted key that has not expired. Revocations are "R" lines in the signed package list (from the Library's revoked.txt) rather than a separate revoked.txt download: refused to install, disabled at the next refresh (db/NAME.disabled, in status, not mounted). docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.9: the groundwork for cellular (1.6.0) and for mobile devices › Part 8: developers, custom builds, and the official recovery (added on 2026-11-11) › 8.2 Publishing to the Library: a chain of trust
docs.t: The sandbox first (a requirement before any outside developer's app): Library web apps are served today from the desktop's own address (127.0.0.1:8080/pkg/...), so a package has the desktop's whole access to rudolfd. That is fine for the project's own Quake and Emu, not for anyone else's. Outside apps run on an origin of their own (rudolfd serves /pkg/<name>/ on a separate port per package, or a sandboxed frame without allow-same-origin), with no rudolfd token, and talk to the desktop only through a small message API granting what their PKGINFO asks and the person allowed: saves (their own folder only), gamepads, full screen, notifications, network (on by default), nothing else. The games plan's rudolf-gamekit uses only this API. Done (2026-11-13): the web-app window's frame has no origin (rudolfd also sends /pkg/ pages with a sandbox policy, so one opened some other way is sandboxed too). The API is the game kit's messages (games58.js, rudolfGame: hello, load, save; the Library's lib/gamekit); the project's own Library apps get them with full screen and controllers as before; an outside developer's app gets what PKGINFO's permissions lists (saves, gamepad, fullscreen) and the person allowed, asked once per account. docs.t: An official recovery slot: (1.5.8 already keeps system/r on every stick Make a stick makes, as the stick's rescue system, and the start-up falls back to it; this part makes it the official recovery everywhere.) Besides the two update slots (a and b), RUDOLFDATA keeps system/r: the newest official release that started successfully on this computer (kernel and layers), with its manifest and signature. rudolf-update fills and refreshes it only from releases signed by the official key, after they have started once (boot-ok), and never from a release signed by an extra key. On a computer that never ran the official build (a developer's own disc), it is downloaded from the official update address the first time Developer mode is on.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.5.9: the groundwork for cellular (1.6.0) and for mobile devices › Part 8: developers, custom builds, and the official recovery (added on 2026-11-11) › 8.4 Recovery mode is always the official Rudolf OS
docs.t: An official recovery start-up file: the ESP keeps /EFI/rudolf/recovery.efi, the official UKI (signed with the official Secure Boot key), and the "Recovery mode" boot entry starts that file, not the normal one (/EFI/rudolf/rudolf.efi, which a custom build replaces). Its initramfs carries the official public key and starts only system/r, after checking its manifest's signature and every file's size and SHA-256; it ignores /persist/etc/rudolf/extra-keys and the update address entirely.
