docs.t: Who asked: the portal watches its own bus (the same user's: the bus's monitoring) for an app calling a Secret Service prompt's Prompt(), which the daemon's question follows, and names that app: its Flatpak ID (the App Store's name for it), else its program (claude: Claude, code: Visual Studio Code, ...), else "An app".

docs.h: Rudolf OS 1.6.0: the first cellular release › Parts › 14. A keyring for Linux apps: the Secret Service (added on 2026-11-14)
docs.t: The question goes to the desktop as the portal's others do (a request in /run/rudolf/portal/req, kind "keyring": the daemon's title, message, description and warning, a new password or not, its choice, its buttons' words), drawn in keyring60.js in Settings' prompt style (the administrator's prompt: 🔑, who asked, the daemon's words as text, the password fields that hide what is typed, a new one asked twice and a mismatch said, the choice as a tick box), in front of the app on the screen (promptFront). The answer (yes with the password, or no) goes back through portal/answer; rudolfd now writes answers 0600 and owned by the user whose portal asked (they were 0644). The portal reads it, wipes it and hands the password to the daemon encrypted. A question the daemon withdraws (the app went away) is removed, and the desktop closes it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › How a native app is built
docs.t: One program per app (/usr/bin/rudolf-APP), started by rudolf-native as any program, framed by its window manager. A small shared library, librudolf-ui (iso/sys/ui/), holds what every app needs and the page already has: the accent colour and its variants (acVariant, acInk: already ported to C in rudolf-native), light and dark, the fonts and sizes of Display Properties, the translations (the page's language files read as they are), dialogs (Open, Save, Confirm in Rudolf's look), the about box, and rudolfd's client (the token, HTTP, JSON: from rudolf-native).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › How a native app is built
docs.t: Files: a native app reads and writes the account's real home folder (opened at sign-in by rudolfd), the same files the web apps see, so a document opened in WordLite's web version and in its native one is one file. Paths are shown as the page shows them (C:\\Users\\NAME\\Documents). Settings and an app's own state go through rudolfd (desktop/settings and a new apps/state?app=NAME), never into the web page's storage directly, so the page (Standard and Lite, still there) and native apps stay in step while both exist.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › How a native app is built
docs.t: The same look (the owner, 2026-11-14: Rudolf OS on Native appears and works exactly as on Standard): a native app is drawn to look like its web version, not like a stock GTK app: librudolf-ui carries a GTK CSS theme made from the page's styles (its buttons, fields, menus, scrollbars, tabs, lists, the accent colour, light and dark), and each app's windows are screenshot-compared with the web version as in docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12's rule (under 2 % of pixels different, text anti-aliasing aside). An app is not switched over until it passes.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › How a native app is built
docs.t: The same behaviour: each app's native version passes a checklist made from its web version (its menus, its shortcuts, its files, its settings, what its browser tests check), screenshots compared side by side under Xvfb. Until an app is native, its web version opens in a one-app WebKit window as in 1.6.0. When the native version passes, the start menu, the pins, file associations and Open with point to it; its web version stays in the page for Standard and Lite until 2.0 decides their future (below).

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › The order
docs.t: Small and much used first, so the way of building is proved on easy apps before the large ones. Wave 1: small apps, proving librudolf-ui Clock (alarms, timers, world clock), Calculator, Notepad, Task Manager (from rudolfd's process list, as now), Image Viewer, Screenshot, Characters & Emoji, Font Viewer, Trash.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › The order
docs.t: Wave 2: the everyday tools File Explorer (its drag and drop with the shell's desktop and windows), Media Player (GStreamer), PDF Viewer (with printing, as 1.5.9's: a PDF renderer is the wave's one new library, poppler-glib, about 5 MB, budget checked), Archive Manager, Command Prompt and Terminal (VTE if it fits the budget, else a terminal of our own on a pty), Code Editor, Event Viewer, Calendar, Contacts, Weather, Voice Recorder, Camera, Help.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › The order
docs.t: Wave 3: the large apps Settings (every page, Search in Settings with its index, Display Properties' previews drawn natively), WordLite, WordPro, SpreadsheetPro, PresentPro, Paint, App Store and Packages, Developer Console, Blitzen, Phone screen. Settings goes first in this wave: it is opened most, and its page costs the most memory today. Staying web pages (decided per app, not rewritten by default) Oracle Browser: a browser is a web engine; it stays Chromium (Standard) or WebKit, framed by the native window manager, its tabs and menus already its own.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › The order
docs.t: The games and creative tools built on the web: Board Games, Card Games, Emu, Flash Player, Quake Engine, GPU Lab, WOS Galaxy Map, BlockLua Builder, and the screen savers: they draw with canvas and WebGL, a native rewrite gains little, and they open in one-app windows. Each is reconsidered after wave 3 with its memory measured.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › Each app's pull request
docs.t: One app per pull request (a large app may take several, each one working), based on main, the owner merging: the program, its host test under Xvfb (iso/qt/native/APP_t.sh: opens, its checklist, screenshots), the start menu and associations switched once it passes, a CHANGELOG line, and its memory at idle with a file open measured against its web version (the PR says both). The release build compiles every native app and fails if one is missing from the base layer or over its budget.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › What 2.0 decides when wave 3 is done
docs.t: Whether Standard and Lite (the web desktop) stay in the system layer as fallbacks, or move to a recovery-only role, or go. Until then they stay, and Native gives up to Standard as in 1.5.9. Whether the web desktop is kept as the browser build (Rudolf OS in a browser tab) and the phone web app, or retired. Wayland (docs/plan-1.5.9.md 12.2: X11 for now): decided with the phone's shell.

docs.h: Rudolf OS 2.0: the apps become native (added on 2026-11-13) › Measurements that close 2.0
docs.t: On the Vivobook, at idle and with the five most used apps open: memory used, start to the desktop, power on battery; against 1.5.9's table. Target: idle under 700 MB used, five apps open under 1 GB.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11)
docs.t: Games made for Rudolf OS, published in the Rudolf OS Library (merciless146/rudolfos-library) and installed from the App Store. They are played first on Rudolf OS computers (keyboard, mouse, controllers), and every one is built so that it runs unchanged on the 1.6.0 mobile version (touch, portrait screens, ARM64, little memory), as all of Rudolf OS's own apps are to. Rudolf OS already has: Checkers and Chess (Board Games), Five-Card Draw, Texas Hold'em, Pai Gow Poker, Hearts and Solitaire (Card Games), Snake, Quake and the emulators (Library), the WOS Galaxy Map, BlockLua, and cloud gaming (Xbox Cloud Gaming, GeForce NOW). These games fill what is missing.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Where they live
docs.t: The code: each game is a webapp package in rudolfos-library (apps/rudolf-<game>/PKGINFO and www/), built, signed with the Library's key and published by its workflow like rudolf-quake and rudolf-emu. Installed, it is mounted at /pkg/rudolf-<game>/ and served by rudolfd; removing it deletes one file. In the system (RudolfOS): a few lines per game, the Start menu and the App Store's Games tab entry with its icon, title and size. Opened without its package, it offers to download it, as Quake does. The system download does not grow with games. This plan: in RudolfOS (docs/plan-games.md), with the version plans.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Rules for every game (desktop now, mobile in 1.6.0)
docs.t: 1. One input layer (a small shared library in the Library, rudolf-gamekit): keyboard, mouse, touch and gamepad at once, mapped to the game's actions. A game never assumes a mouse or a keyboard; on-screen controls appear only when touch is used. 2. Any window shape: the playfield scales to the window, portrait included (tablet mode, 1.5.8; phones, 1.6.0). 3. Speed: 60 frames a second drawn by the processor alone, Canvas 2D, no graphics card needed. The yardstick is the Vivobook on the Lite desktop (WebKit, software drawing). The same code on Chromium and WebKit. 4. Size: under about 2 MB per game, everything inside the package; nothing downloaded while playing.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Rules for every game (desktop now, mobile in 1.6.0)
docs.t: 5. Saves: through rudolfd's mirror (they follow the account and are backed up), with export and import as a file. 6. Pausing: on the lock screen, the screen saver, a call (1.5.9 Part 7), a notification the person opens, the window covered or minimised, and on a phone when the app goes to the background. 7. Offline: everything works without a connection; online leaderboards only where a game has them, and optional. 8. Accessibility: difficulty levels, a reduce-flashing setting, colours that do not rely on red and green alone, remappable keys and buttons, captions for any spoken or important sound.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Rules for every game (desktop now, mobile in 1.6.0)
docs.t: 9. Original work: original names, art, music and rules where rules are protected; no assets from other games. The falling-blocks game does not use the name or look of any trademarked game.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › The games › Night Flight (the only Christmas-themed game)
docs.t: A top-down, vertically scrolling bullet-hell shooter. Rudolf, the OS's mascot, flies up through a portrait playfield and fires lasers from his nose. Play Nose laser: tap or hold to fire a rapid stream; hold longer to charge a piercing beam. "Glow" pick-ups upgrade it (wider spread, then homing shots). Focus: hold a key (or a second finger) to move slowly; Rudolf's small hitbox, a glowing point at his nose, shows, for threading through dense patterns. Glow Burst (the bomb): a few per life; clears the bullets on screen and briefly turns corrupted enemies back to their colours. Grazing: passing close to bullets fills a meter for score and extra bombs.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › The games › Night Flight (the only Christmas-themed game)
docs.t: Bosses: one at the end of each stage, with phases and named bullet patterns. Rescues: corrupted friends can be saved (hit with a Glow Burst or the charged beam) for bonuses and extra lives. Modes: Story (6 stages), Practice (any stage reached, slow-motion assist), Score Attack, and after the ending a lighter "Restored" mode. The light-to-dark arc 1. Stages 1-2: a bright, colourful winter night: twinkling lights, candy colours, friendly villagers and workshop helpers. The first corrupted enemies are few and easy to read against the colour. 2. Stages 3-4: the corruption spreads: colours drain, lights flicker and glitch, friends begin to turn.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › The games › Night Flight (the only Christmas-themed game)
docs.t: 3. Stages 5-6: dark and corrupted: deep purples and blacks, static, inverted ornaments, cracked toys and twisted machinery, bullets in sickly glowing colours; the final boss is the source of the corruption. Clearing the game brings the colour back to every stage. Art direction

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › The games › Night Flight (the only Christmas-themed game)
docs.t: Rudolf and the friendly characters: soft and cartoonish, child-friendly, in the spirit of open-source mascots such as Linux's Tux (without copying any of them): round shapes built from circles and ovals, no sharp corners; a big head and a small chubby body, short legs, stubby antlers with rounded tips; large friendly eyes with highlights, a small smile; Rudolf's nose glows warmly and pulses brighter as the laser charges. A few flat, warm, bright colours, a soft outline, one highlight and one shadow tone. Bouncy, squashy animation: Rudolf wobbles as he dodges, blinks, and cheers when a friend is rescued. Villagers, workshop helpers and small woodland animals in the same style.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › The games › Night Flight (the only Christmas-themed game)
docs.t: Corrupted characters: sinister, still simple enough to read at speed: angular and jagged silhouettes, cracks, thorny edges, uneven limbs; narrow glowing eyes (toxic purple, red or green) without highlights; dark, desaturated bodies with sickly glowing accents, flickering static and "corruption" dripping at the edges; jerky, glitching animation. A turning friend changes step by step from the round, colourful version to the sharp, dark one, and pops back when rescued, so the corruption is seen, not told. Child-friendly: creepy, not gory: no blood, nothing grotesque; beaten enemies burst into sparkles and static; bosses are menacing by shape, size and colour, not violence. The reduce-flashing setting tones the glitch effects down.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › The games › Night Flight (the only Christmas-themed game)
docs.t: Rudolf's own design: Rudolf is Rudolf OS's own character. Kept clearly distinct from Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer (a trademarked character): Rudolf OS's own antler shape, colours, proportions and style, and nothing from that story (Santa's reindeer team, its well-known characters, songs or places). The nose laser is a mechanic, not a borrowing. Worth a check by someone qualified before the game is published. Controls Desktop: arrows or WASD to move, Z to fire (hold to charge), Shift for focus, X for Glow Burst, Esc to pause; a controller (left stick or d-pad, A fire, right trigger focus, B bomb).

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › The games › Night Flight (the only Christmas-themed game)
docs.t: Phone (1.6.0): drag anywhere to steer (Rudolf follows the finger at an offset, so the finger does not hide him), fire is automatic, a second finger held for focus, a two-finger tap for Glow Burst. Technical Canvas 2D; bullets in fixed pools (no allocation while playing); circle hit tests; a fixed time step, so runs are deterministic and replays can be saved and watched. Up to about 600 bullets on screen on the Vivobook on Lite; more where the computer allows (measured at start-up and in the settings). The corruption effects (palette shifts, scanlines, glitch slices) drawn cheaply in Canvas; none needs a graphics card.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › The games › Night Flight (the only Christmas-themed game)
docs.t: Sound: Web Audio, short effects and looped music in Opus, all inside the package (about 2 MB in all as the target).

docs.t: 1. 1.5.9: rudolf-gamekit (input, scaling, saves, pausing); then Fault Lines, Block Drop, Logic Pack and Night Flight (stages 1-2 and the engine first; stages 3-6 when the art for the corruption is settled). docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Progress
docs.t: 2026-11-11: Frost Barricade (asked for; for older players, cartoon horror and combat): an original barricade-defence shooter, apps/rudolf-frostbarricade (about 26 KB as a package). Corrupted elves in Night Flight's style, nine winter weapons, days of repair, search and training, survivors, fifteen nights; the rescuer on Night 15 is an original character, Captain Quill (a rockhopper penguin in a red winter coat, with a sleigh pulled by snowy owls), not another project's mascot. tests/frostbarricade_t.js (26 checks). In LIB_GAMES.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Progress
docs.t: 2026-11-12: Block Drop (apps/rudolf-blockdrop, about 20 KB as a package). Its own rules and look, not a copy of a trademarked game: an 8-wide, 16-deep well; pieces of three and four blocks; colours that do not follow the shape, each with its own mark (circle, triangle, square, diamond, cross). The twist: every 12th piece carries a prism; where it lands, every block of its colour bursts, the blocks above tumble down their columns, and rows that fill clear in a chain (worth more each step); while it falls, the blocks it would burst are outlined. Classic (faster every 10 rows), Relaxed (one speed), Daily (3 minutes, the same blocks for everyone). Touch: drag to move, tap to turn, flick down to drop, and a touch bar; on a tall window the panel moves above the well. tests/blockdrop_t.js (33 checks). In LIB_GAMES. Next: Logic Pack.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Progress
docs.t: 2026-11-12: Logic Pack (apps/rudolf-logicpack, about 24 KB as a package): Sudoku, Picture Grid (nonograms) and Cages (Latin squares with + − × ÷ cages), made in the game (logic.js, under 25 ms each), each with exactly one answer. Sudoku Easy solves with naked singles, Medium with hidden singles too, Hard is only unique; Picture Grid 5×5, 10×10, 15×15, solvable line by line (a cell is given where line logic stalls); Cages 4×4 to 6×6. A Daily puzzle per kind. Notes, undo, clashes and wrong cages marked (with a bar, not colour alone), clues greyed when their line matches, hints that fix a wrong entry or do the next step and say why; each kind's puzzle in progress kept. The pad goes under the grid on a tall window. tests/logicpack_t.js (41 checks). In LIB_GAMES. Next (1.5.9-1.6.0): Wordsmith, Galaxy Conquest, FreeCell and Spider, Chess levels.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Frost Barricade 1.1: twenty-five nights, the weather radio, the weather, wendigos
docs.t: Asked for on 2026-11-11 and built (rudolfos-library#6, on #5's eye colours, bloaters and muggers). Twenty-five nights; the sleigh comes at the end of the last, in the great blizzard. A prep screen before every night with a weather radio: tonight's weather and tomorrow night's, a warning the day before a blizzard, and on Day 22 always the warning of the three-night blizzard. The schedule, fixed per game from its seed: days 1-7 clear or fog; a blizzard on day 8 or 9 and on 17 or 18 (the other day clear or fog); the great blizzard on 23-25; one full moon (20% a day on days 8-14, 60% on 15-20, 80% on 21, otherwise 22), never on a blizzard's day.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Frost Barricade 1.1: twenty-five nights, the weather radio, the weather, wendigos
docs.t: Clear: full sight; searching goes quicker. Full moon: brighter; every white-eyed elf becomes a red-eyed sprinter; a wendigo comes. Fog: sight is a cone of light from Rudolf's nose towards the crosshair; elves out of it show as ripples of sound; their sounds louder; searching finds less and scouts are more often lost. Blizzard: a shorter, narrower cone; no ripples; nothing sprints; the survivors' aim suffers; no searching.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Frost Barricade 1.1: twenty-five nights, the weather radio, the weather, wendigos
docs.t: The wendigo (reworked in 1.2): a mini-boss, always red-eyed; a screech (and a caption) a few seconds before it appears; huge, very tough and slow, drifting towards Rudolf's lane; only one on the field at a time. Every 5-8 s it stops for 1.5 s to draw in a screech, then lets it go down its lane with the screen shaking: it hurts survivors in its path (not the barricade), and if it reaches Rudolf he is stunned, his sight blurs and his ears ring, fully for 3 s, then fading. One under the full moon, one on Night 24, two on Night 25 (one after the other). An original design: gaunt, long-limbed, sharp branching antlers, frightening by shape rather than gore.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Frost Barricade 1.2: shielders and Bash
docs.t: Asked for on 2026-11-11 and built (rudolfos-library#7). Shielders: cyan eyes, above-average health, from Night 5. Their shield covers the waist, chest and head (not the lower legs and feet) and stops every shot, survivors' bolts included; piercing shots stop at it; fire reaches round it for half. Explosives and Bash knock it loose and the shielder back. From Night 10 a shielder goes back for its own shield; from Night 18 an ordinary white-eyed elf walking over a fallen shielder's shield may take it up (it keeps its white eyes and its own health).

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › Holiday Holdout (25 Days 1.3.1)
docs.t: Asked for on 2026-11-15: 25 Days is renamed Holiday Holdout (the package stays rudolf-frostbarricade): its package title, page title and title screen (rudolfos-library), and the Games list here (desktop/games58.js).

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › 25 Days (Frost Barricade 1.3)
docs.t: Asked for on 2026-11-12. The game is renamed 25 Days (the package stays rudolf-frostbarricade, so saves carry on). A grittier look, like the old violent Flash games: darker, washed-out colours, film grain and a vignette, dead trees and fence posts, dark ichor splatter, tumbling chunks and stains that last the night, muzzle smoke and spent casings. Rudolf redrawn after Rudolf OS's portrait (the boot splash): an angular, faceted white stag with branching antlers, a diamond ear, a slanted eye, a ruff and the red nose, full body, with a bandolier.

docs.h: Rudolf OS games: a plan (asked for on 2026-11-11) › 25 Days (Frost Barricade 1.3)
docs.t: A wider field and lanes, a longer barricade. Rudolf moves up and down behind it (W/S, the arrows, a controller's left stick, a drag behind the barricade) and aims within 15 degrees of level. Shots fly on past the crosshair until an elf or a shield stops them; the Ornament Launcher still bursts at the crosshair. Unlimited ammunition, quicker reloads (searching finds scrap instead of ammunition); the elves 30% faster, the sprinters most (the wendigo unchanged). The survivors shoot each in their own time, about 40% hits untrained to 85% trained; below 5% of the barricade they panic, drop their crossbows and run until morning.

docs.t: Apps made for Rudolf OS that not everyone needs move out of the system into an online catalog, from which the App Store downloads them, like Flathub for Linux apps. Apps made for Rudolf OS later go there too.

The few kilobytes of each app's own desktop code stay, so Quake and Emu stay in the Start menu and the Games tab; opened without their package, they offer to download it.

docs.h: The Rudolf OS Library: a catalog of apps made for Rudolf OS (planned for 1.5.2) › How it works: rpk, which Rudolf OS already has
docs.t: rpk (iso/sys/rpk.c) is Rudolf OS's package manager since 1.3.0: a package is a read-only squashfs image with an Ed25519 signature; installed packages are mounted at /pkg/<name>, so installing never changes the system and removing one deletes one file; kinds: webapp (www/ served by rudolfd at /pkg/<name>/, opened in a desktop window), addon (files the desktop uses), app, cli; a repository is static files: index.txt (one package per line) and index.sig, plus the packages; sources: the disc's own repository and lines in /persist/pkg/sources. The Library is an rpk repository on the internet, added to every computer's sources. Packages: rudolf-quake (addon): the files now in www/rudolfq, served at /pkg/rudolf-quake/www/; rudolf-emu (addon): the emulators now in www/lib/emu.

docs.h: The Rudolf OS Library: a catalog of apps made for Rudolf OS (planned for 1.5.2) › How it works: rpk, which Rudolf OS already has
docs.t: The desktop looks for them at /pkg/<name>/ instead of in its own folder.

docs.h: The Rudolf OS Library: a catalog of apps made for Rudolf OS (planned for 1.5.2) › Where it lives: a GitHub repository, yes, a separate one
docs.t: A GitHub repository is the right home, and a separate one, merciless146/rudolfos-library, is better than a folder in RudolfOS. Why GitHub: Hosting at no cost, and no server to run. The packages go in GitHub Releases (files up to 2 GB each), and the signed index in GitHub Pages. Rudolf OS's own updates already work this way, so nothing new needs to be learned or paid for. The host does not need to be trusted. rpk checks every package's signature against keys built into Rudolf OS, so a database server or anything more would add nothing. A build workflow (Actions) packs, signs and publishes each app, and keeps the history of every version. Why separate from RudolfOS:

docs.h: The Rudolf OS Library: a catalog of apps made for Rudolf OS (planned for 1.5.2) › Where it lives: a GitHub repository, yes, a separate one
docs.t: Its own schedule. A new version of an app is published by itself, without a Rudolf OS release, and every computer gets it through the App Store's updates. Its own key. See below: if the Library's key were ever stolen, it could not sign a system update. Room for others. People who make apps for Rudolf OS can later be given access to the Library repository without any access to the operating system or its keys. A clean RudolfOS repository, whose gh-pages branch holds only the system's update channels.

docs.h: The Rudolf OS Library: a catalog of apps made for Rudolf OS (planned for 1.5.2) › Where it lives: a GitHub repository, yes, a separate one
docs.t: Layout of rudolfos-library: ` apps/<name>/PKGINFO name, version, kind, title, description, icon, licence, category apps/<name>/www/... the app's files (or a fetch script for large data, pinned by SHA-256) .github/workflows/publish.yml build each changed app, sign it, upload it to a release, update the signed index ` Published: https://merciless146.github.io/rudolfos-library/index.txt, index.sig and catalog.json (titles, icons, descriptions, sizes, for the App Store), with the packages next to them (<name>.rpk). (As built: rpk takes each package's file from the same place as the list, so the packages are on Pages too, not in Releases.)

docs.h: The Rudolf OS Library: a catalog of apps made for Rudolf OS (planned for 1.5.2) › Keys: the Library gets its own
docs.t: Today /etc/rudolf/rpk-keys is trusted by both rpk (packages) and rudolf-update (the system's updates). A key added there for the Library could also sign a system update. So: a new Ed25519 key pair for the Library, made by you with the existing tool (as the release key was); its public key in a new file, /etc/rudolf/library-keys, which rpk trusts and rudolf-update does not. The release key keeps signing system updates only.

docs.h: The Rudolf OS Library: a catalog of apps made for Rudolf OS (planned for 1.5.2) › The App Store and the desktop
docs.t: A Rudolf OS Library tab in the App Store: each app with its icon, size, description and licence, and Get / Open / Remove / Update. Opening Quake or Emu without the package: "Quake is in the Rudolf OS Library (13 MB). Download it?", and it opens when the download finishes. Nobody loses an app: on the first start of 1.5.2, a computer whose Games folder or saves show it used Quake or Emu gets that package installed by itself (in the background, when online), with a notification.

docs.h: The Rudolf OS Library: a catalog of apps made for Rudolf OS (planned for 1.5.2) › The App Store and the desktop
docs.t: Offline: the disc image's own repository carries both packages, so an install from the disc or a live session can add them without internet. The download of the system shrinks, and the disc stays the same size. Updates: the App Store's Updates also checks the Library; the health log records installs and updates.

docs.h: The Rudolf OS Library: a catalog of apps made for Rudolf OS (planned for 1.5.2) › Steps
docs.t: 2. rudolfos-library: the layout, the publish workflow, the two packages; first publish. 3. Rudolf OS 1.5.2: - /etc/rudolf/library-keys, rpk trusting it, and the Library added to sources; - Quake and Emu reading their files from /pkg/; - the Library tab; - "download it?" when an app is missing; - reinstalling for computers that used them; - the disc repository carrying both packages; - www/rudolfq and www/lib/emu removed from the desktop layer. 4. Tests: - in the browser: the Library tab, download prompts, reinstall on update; - in QEMU: install from the Library over the network and from the disc, Quake and Emu running from /pkg/, removal; - a system update signed with the Library key is refused.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12)
docs.t: Why: on the Vivobook (3.4 GB, AMD 0x1506), Standard at idle uses about 1.0 to 1.2 GB, and about 200 to 250 MB of it belongs to no process (docs/plan-1.5.9.md Part 10). On budget and old computers that is a large share. The only place that says what it is, is the kernel's debug files (debugfs): the graphics driver's page pool, every graphics buffer with the process that owns it, and the buffers shared between processes. With Secure Boot on, the start-up locks the kernel down (integrity), and lockdown keeps debugfs closed. So the reading needs one start with Secure Boot off, then Secure Boot back on. Nothing in Rudolf OS changes for it, and no release ever ships without lockdown.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › What is safe about it, and what is given up for that start
docs.t: Turning Secure Boot off in the firmware keeps the Rudolf OS key: it is in shim's key list (MOK), not the firmware's own keys. Rudolf OS starts as before (docs/secure-boot.md: "With Secure Boot off everything works as before, and the layers are still checked"). For that one start: unsigned kernel modules and kernels could load, and kernel memory could be read or written by root. Nothing does that in Rudolf OS, but the start should do nothing else: no browsing, no downloads, no USB script below, which reads.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › What is safe about it, and what is given up for that start
docs.t: Never choose "Reset to setup mode", "Clear Secure Boot keys" or "Restore factory keys" in the firmware: that could remove the keys the firmware checks shim with. Only the one switch, Secure Boot on/off. The test-only start options (RUDOLF_UKI_TEST_CMDLINE and the test keys) are not used: the release's own signed start, with Secure Boot off, is all that is needed.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › Steps
docs.t: 1. Before (Secure Boot on): the final 1.5.8 installed, Standard, signed in, nothing open, five minutes idle. The usual read (memgap.sh) for the baseline: the in-use figure, the processes, the gap. 2. Secure Boot off: restart into the firmware (on Asus laptops usually F2 at the logo, then Advanced mode › Security › Secure Boot › Secure Boot Control: Disabled), save and restart. Sign in, open nothing, five minutes idle. 3. Check the start: lockdown reads [none] and the gap is about the same as in step 1 (the same start, only unlocked). If the gap is very different, the comparison is off: stop and note it.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › Steps
docs.t: 4. Read, three times (memdbg.sh, read-only: it mounts debugfs read-only, reads, unmounts): - idle: as it is; - video: a YouTube video full screen in Oracle for two minutes, then the reading while it plays; - closed: the video's tab closed, two minutes, then the last reading (what stays after use). The script refuses to read anything if lockdown is on. 5. Secure Boot back on, the same switch: restart into the firmware, Secure Boot Control: Enabled, save, restart.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › Steps
docs.t: 6. Check it is back: lockdown reads [integrity], /etc/rudolf/secureboot is 1, and Task Manager › System and Settings › Security say Secure Boot is on. If the computer does not start with it on, the key was lost: enroll it again (MokManager, docs/secure-boot.md), never leave it off. The whole start without lockdown takes about 20 minutes.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › What is read
docs.t: TTM page pool (ttm/page_pool): pages the graphics driver keeps for reuse after buffers are freed. Counted as used, owned by no process. Graphics buffers by process (dri/*/amdgpu_gem_info): every buffer, in VRAM (the 256 MB carve-out) or in GTT (system memory the graphics card uses), with its owner: Chromium's GPU process, the compositor (cage), Xwayland. Memory managers (amdgpu_vram_mm, amdgpu_gtt_mm): how much of each is handed out. Shared buffers (dma_buf/bufinfo): buffers passed between processes (the screen's own, video frames). With them, as before: meminfo, slab, vmalloc by caller.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › What each answer leads to
docs.t: | Where the gap is | What it means | What can be done (1.5.9 or later) | |---|---|---| | The TTM pool | freed graphics memory kept for reuse | cap the pool (ttm.page_pool_size) for small computers; measure the frame rate before and after | | GTT buffers of Chromium's GPU process | the desktop page's layers and textures | Part 10 (a lighter page), fewer layers (the overlays only when shown), Chromium's GPU memory limits | | GTT buffers of cage or Xwayland | the screen's buffers | fewer screen buffers (double rather than triple), Xwayland only when an X app runs | | Shared video buffers | frames kept after the video | check they are freed when the tab closes (the closed reading) | | Slab or vmalloc | the kernel itself | the driver or module named, and its options |

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › What each answer leads to
docs.t: The findings go into docs/plan-1.5.9.md (Part 10, or a new part), with the readings.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › What the first reading found (2026-11-12, released 1.5.8, 2026111219)
docs.t: | Reading | In use | Unaccounted | Graphics pool (TTM) | Graphics in system memory (GTT) | |---|---|---|---|---| | idle | 1,074 MB | 198 MB | 21 MB | 17 MB | | a video full screen | 1,906 MB | 245 MB | 27 MB | 38 MB | | two minutes after closing Oracle | 1,228 MB | 206 MB | 46 MB | 19 MB | Graphics buffers are small (the X server about 27 MB, Chromium's GPU process 8 to 23 MB, mostly in the 256 MB of the graphics card's own memory); no shared buffers (dma-buf) at all.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › What the first reading found (2026-11-12, released 1.5.8, 2026111219)
docs.t: The graphics pool grows a little with use (21 → 46 MB) and its limit is 1.7 GB: a cap (64 MB) goes into 1.5.9. 140 to 180 MB is neither graphics nor any counter: memory taken page by page by the kernel or a driver, there from the start and steady. This kernel has nothing that names it (no /proc/allocinfo, no page_owner).

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › Part 2: a test kernel that names it
docs.t: The workflow *Test kernel* (iso/systools/testkernel.sh) builds the stable release's kernel with allocation profiling (MEM_ALLOC_PROFILING, on from the start) and its own modules layer, as the pre-release test-allocinfo. No update ever installs it. On the Vivobook, with Secure Boot off again (the same switch): and its modules, and the base, Chromium and desktop layers of the running slot (hard links, no extra room). 2. The running system hands over to the test kernel (sync, file systems read-only, kexec with rudolf.slot=r): the same start as an update's, without the firmware. The modules layer is not the release's, so it starts as "unchecked", which only a start with Secure Boot off allows.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › Part 2: a test kernel that names it
docs.t: 3. Five minutes idle, then /proc/allocinfo is read (read-only): every place in the kernel with how much it holds, the largest first, along with the counters above. 4. A normal restart (the released kernel again), the slot r removed, and Secure Boot back on and checked. Nothing else on the drive changes; if the test kernel does not start, the power button and a normal start bring the released system back.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › What the test kernel found (2026-11-12, idle, 204 MB unaccounted)
docs.t: /proc/allocinfo on the Vivobook, five minutes idle (the test kernel through slot r, Secure Boot off): | Held by | MB | What it is | |---|---|---| | drivers/iommu/dma-iommu.c (__iommu_dma_alloc_pages) | 65 | the SSD's host memory buffer: the Kingston OM8PGP4128P has no DRAM of its own and borrows 64 MiB (nvme0: allocated 64 MiB host memory buffer) | | ttm_pool_alloc_page [ttm] | 42 | the graphics driver's pool and the graphics card's system memory | | net/core/skbuff.c (kmalloc_reserve) | 16 | network (Wi-Fi) receive buffers | | blk-mq requests, dm-bufio | 9 | the drive's requests; dm-verity's cache of checked blocks | | IOMMU tables, smaller | 5 | |

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › What the test kernel found (2026-11-12, idle, 204 MB unaccounted)
docs.t: About 135 of the 204 MB is named; the other 60 to 70 MB was taken before tracking could see it (early start-up). Nothing is a leak and nothing is wasted by Rudolf OS. The largest part is the hardware of a budget laptop: an SSD without DRAM borrows RAM, and it is faster for it. Limiting it (nvme.max_host_mem_size_mb) would trade the drive's speed for 64 MB: left as it is. The graphics pool cap stays in 1.5.9 (Part 10); the network and drive buffers are normal and small. The memory to win is the desktop page's (Part 10), not hidden memory.

docs.h: Finding the hidden memory: one start without lockdown (planned 2026-11-12) › What the test kernel found (2026-11-12, idle, 204 MB unaccounted)
docs.t: After the reading: a normal restart into the released kernel, slot r and the test files removed, Secure Boot back on and checked (lockdown [integrity], 2026111219 from slot b). The pre-release test-allocinfo stays for a later measurement; it is never in a channel. The test kernel's screen was garbled: handing over by kexec from a running desktop leaves the graphics card set up hand over before any graphics driver has started, so they are not affected.

docs.h: Secure Boot
docs.t: Rudolf OS 1.2.2 starts on UEFI computers with Secure Boot on. This page says how, and what to do when a part of it has to change.

docs.h: Secure Boot › The chain
docs.t: | Step | File on the disc's UEFI image | Checked by | Signed with | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI, shim (Ubuntu's shim-signed) | the firmware (Microsoft's UEFI CA, in every PC) | Microsoft | | 2 | EFI/BOOT/grubx64.efi, systemd-boot: the boot menu | shim: the key enrolled in its key list (MOK) | the Rudolf OS key | | 3 | EFI/rudolf/rudolf.efi, the kernel bundle: systemd's stub, the kernel with its initramfs, fixed options | shim, through systemd-boot | the Rudolf OS key | | 3r | EFI/rudolf/recovery.efi (1.5.9), the official recovery start-up file, started by the menu's Recovery mode: the same kernel and a second initramfs in the bundle (the recovery mark and the official release key alone); it starts only system/r on RUDOLFDATA after checking its signed release list with that key and every file's size and SHA-256 (never Developer mode's extra key) | shim, through systemd-boot | the Rudolf OS key | | 4 | the system layers (RUDOLF/*.SFS) | dm-verity, against the root hashes in the signed release list RUDOLF/MANIFEST.TXT | the release key (Ed25519) | | 5 | an updated kernel in a slot on RUDOLFDATA (kexec) | the running kernel: the Rudolf

docs.h: Secure Boot › The chain
docs.t: OS certificate is built in as trusted | the Rudolf OS key | MokManager (EFI/BOOT/mmx64.efi) is where a person enrolls the Rudolf OS key the first time (EFI/rudolf/rudolf.cer), or confirms the request made by Settings > Security Settings > Prepare Secure Boot (rudolfd: POST /api/secureboot/prepare, MokNew and MokAuth with a one-time password).

docs.h: Secure Boot › The chain
docs.t: With Secure Boot on, the initramfs locks the kernel down (integrity) before anything else runs: unsigned modules (all modules are signed when the kernel is built, with a key made for that build), unsigned kernels (kexec) and writing to kernel memory are refused. A layer that fails its check, or a missing signed list, stops the start-up with a restart instead of a shell. rudolfd ignores the desktop page on RUDOLFDATA (os/current), which nothing checks. The boot menu's options are not taken from the menu (the stub ignores them under Secure Boot); the initramfs reads which entry was chosen from the firmware variable LoaderEntrySelected and adds the matching option (rudolf.recovery=1, rudolf.check=1, rudolf.toram=1; rudolf.debug=1 only with Secure Boot off).

docs.h: Secure Boot › The chain
docs.t: With Secure Boot off everything works as before, and the layers are still checked: a damaged one is caught, but an unchecked one may start (Task Manager > System says so). BIOS computers start as before (Rudolf Boot). 32-bit UEFI computers are not supported with Secure Boot on.

docs.h: Secure Boot › Keys
docs.t: Rudolf OS Secure Boot key (RSA-2048): made by iso/systools/mksbkey.sh on the maintainer's computer. iso/boot/sb/rudolf-sb.crt. The release build checks that they match (systools/sbkeycheck.py). If the key is ever replaced, every computer must enroll the new certificate (MokManager) before it starts with Secure Boot on. keys in iso/trusted-keys.txt.

docs.h: Secure Boot › Keeping shim current
docs.t: The parts a disc ships are pinned in iso/boot/sb/parts.txt and kept in the draft release sb-parts by the workflow *Secure Boot parts*. Microsoft revokes old shims from time to time (SBAT and the firmware's revocation list); a disc with a revoked shim no longer starts with Secure Boot on. Then: run *Secure Boot parts*, check the new versions in sb-parts.txt of that release, put the new hashes in parts.txt, and make a new disc. Rudolf OS's own SBAT line (rudolf,1, in systools/mkuki.py) is raised if a Rudolf OS kernel bundle must be withdrawn.

docs.h: System reports
docs.t: How a problem reported from Rudolf OS reaches this repository, and how to work with it.

docs.h: System reports › The path of a report
docs.t: 1. On the computer. The person chooses *Report a problem*: Task Manager (bottom right), or Start › Report a problem. They give it a title and say what happened; *Include the system report* is on by default.

docs.h: System reports › The path of a report
docs.t: 2. The system report (sysReport() in desktop/tm26.js) describes the computer at that moment: - Status: Rudolf OS version and installed release, when the report was made, how the computer started (BIOS or UEFI; disc, USB drive or hard disk; live or installed; recovery), whether the desktop runs in the shell or in the plain page (and whether the shell failed), the display mode and size, uptime and load, CPU use, memory and swap, temperature, battery, free storage, network connected or not, the services, open windows and real tabs, and the number of kernel warnings. - Computer: machine and firmware, processor, graphics card and driver, sound cards, storage, network adapters (kind, state, speed), input devices. - Kernel: version, start-up options, drivers, memory in detail. - Processes: the ten using the most memory, the busiest, and the memory of each page (desktop, tabs). - Latest: kernel warnings and errors, the session log, the shell's notes, the desktop's errors.

docs.h: System reports › The path of a report
docs.t: It leaves out what identifies the person: account names, file names, web addresses, network (IP) and hardware (MAC) addresses, e-mail addresses and Wi-Fi network names. The person can read it before sending (*See the report*), save it to C:\DOCUMENTS instead, or leave it out.

docs.h: System reports › The path of a report
docs.t: 3. GitHub. *Continue on GitHub* opens a new issue in Oracle (real tabs keep the GitHub sign-in) with the form .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/system-report.yml filled in through the address: title, *What happened*, version, *Status at the time* and *Full system report*. GitHub refuses very long addresses, so when the full report does not fit, Rudolf OS puts it on the clipboard and the form says to paste it. The person reviews and submits; nothing is sent before that. A GitHub account is needed. Without internet, the dialog says to save the report and send it later.

docs.h: System reports › The path of a report
docs.t: 4. The database. The workflow .github/workflows/system-reports.yml (script .github/scripts/system-reports.js) runs for every issue labelled system-report when it is opened, edited, closed or reopened, and files it in the system-reports branch: - reports/<issue>.json: the record: number, title, link, author, dates, state, version, the problem, every status line (status), and the full report text; - index.json: one line per report, newest first (state, date, version, how it started, desktop, display, memory, warnings, labels), for tools and scripts; - README.md: open reports by version and by area, and a table of all reports, to read on GitHub.

docs.h: System reports › The path of a report
docs.t: It adds labels (version: 1.2.0, area: sound, area: shell when the shell failed, needs: system report when the status is missing) and, for a new issue, a comment with the key status lines.

docs.h: System reports › Working with reports
docs.t: See them: the issues labelled system-report, or the system-reports branch's README for the overview. Filter by version: … and area: … labels. Address one: reply on the issue, fix the area labels if the guess was wrong, link the fix (Fixes #N in the pull request), and close it when the fix is released. Closing updates its state in the database. Missing status: the comment asks the person to paste *Task Manager › Copy system report*; editing the issue files the new text. Look across reports: index.json has every report in one file, for example curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/merciless146/RudolfOS/system-reports/index.json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="open") | .desktop' | sort | uniq -c.

docs.h: System reports › Safety
docs.t: The issue text is written by anyone. The workflow only reads it as data: it is parsed, trimmed and escaped (the README cannot gain links or images from it), the labels come from a fixed list, and nothing from it is run. The workflow has only contents: write and issues: write, writes only the system-reports branch, and takes its script from the default branch. Reports are public. The report leaves out personal details, but the person's own text and anything they paste are theirs to check; the form says so.

docs.h: System reports › Changing the report
docs.t: Add a line to key in sysReport() for something every report should show (it lands in *Status at the time* and, as Key: value, in the record's status), or a section below for details. Field ids in the form (what, version, status, report) are what the desktop fills in; keep them when editing the form.

docs.h: Testing rules for Rudolf OS
docs.t: Written on 2026-11-10 (plan 1.5.8, item 5.4), after the Lite desktop engine passed every check and then closed as it started on the first real computer it reached.

docs.h: Testing rules for Rudolf OS › Anything that changes how the computer or the desktop starts
docs.t: This covers the start-up (initramfs/init), rudolf-init, the session, the desktop engine, the shell, the display (Xorg, Xvfb, rudolf-display), system updates and the boot files. 1. The fallback comes first. Before the change itself reaches a computer, there is a way back that needs no working desktop, and it is tested: a failing desktop engine gives way to the standard one (qt/host/deskfall57_t.sh), a system slot that cannot start gives way to the previous one (qt/host/startfall57_t.sh), and a stick's rescue system to it when none can (startfall58_t.sh), Recovery mode starts the installed system with safe settings (1.5.9: from recovery.efi, only the official system/r once checked, qt/host/recoveryefi59_t.sh, and in QEMU with Secure Boot, qt/sb/recovery_sb_t.sh), and Ctrl+Alt+Backspace starts the safe desktop (qt/host/desksafe58_t.sh).

docs.h: Testing rules for Rudolf OS › Anything that changes how the computer or the desktop starts
docs.t: 2. Test it from the system itself, not from the build machine. A program run on the release machine finds that machine's libraries. Run it from the built layer (a chroot of base.sfs, as webkit-check.yml does), so a library it opens while running (dlopen: graphics, sound, plug-ins) and the layer lacks fails the check. ldd does not see those.

docs.h: Testing rules for Rudolf OS › Anything that changes how the computer or the desktop starts
docs.t: 3. Test it on the real graphics path. Xvfb and LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE hide what the GPU path does. Before such a change reaches the test laptop, it runs once on Xorg with a GPU (QEMU with virtio-gpu, or the laptop over the showed "Couldn't open libGLESv2.so.2" at once). logs are kept (var/log/starts, System health › Last starts), so a start that never reaches the desktop can be read at the next one.

docs.h: Testing rules for Rudolf OS › Everything else
docs.t: Host tests (qt/host/*_t.sh) for scripts and C helpers, with the paths they use moved into a temporary folder. Browser tests (qt/shell2/*_t.js) for the desktop, each on its own port. QEMU only where it is needed: installing, Encrypt my data, moving to a disk, updates and rollback, and the final set before a release is promoted. python3 systools/deadcheck.py (in iso/) before every pull request.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes
docs.t: Each version's first line after "Summary:" is what Settings shows before an update is installed; the list is what "What's new" and the notification after an update show. The newest version comes first.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: Devices are now set up by udev, as on other Linux distributions, so Linux apps, Steam and the modem service find hardware the usual way; mdev stays as a fallback if udev cannot start.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: The keyring's own questions are now asked by Rudolf OS: when an app creates a new keyring or needs one unlocked, the desktop asks for its password in Rudolf's own prompt, naming the app, instead of the request failing.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: Settings › Privacy › Saved passwords for apps: see which apps keep sign-ins in this account's keyring and remove them; Flatpak apps can now keep theirs too (the Secret portal).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: App Store › Rudolf OS Library says when its list of apps was last checked (and when the Library published it), with a Refresh button at the end of its first line: the list was kept until it stopped working, so a working list days old never showed new apps or updates (Ember Reach on the Vivobook, 2026-11-14)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: A keyring for Linux apps: apps such as the Claude app, VS Code and other Electron apps now keep their sign-ins in the account's own keyring (the Secret Service), unlocked by signing in, instead of warning that GNOME Keyring is not set up or asking again after every restart.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: Settings › System health › Log video problems works on the native desktop too (its video and sound warnings, and Oracle's video and sound messages there), and the native desktop's log is now kept across a restart and included in the system report.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: Planned: what 1.5.9 had left, moved here on 2026-11-15 (docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 15): the native desktop's comparison with Standard, the official recovery's repair at each start, the Vivobook's call and feature checks, QEMU security checks, Lite's tab fixes, the hotspot, ARM64's test channel, Waydroid and the first phone.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: Planned: a keyring for Linux apps (the Secret Service), unlocked by the account's sign-in, so apps such as the Claude app keep their sign-ins without a plain file or a second password.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 4): workspaces as on Standard: the taskbar's 1 2 3 buttons, Ctrl+Alt+Left and Right (with Shift the window goes too), a window's Move to workspace N, the taskbar listing the shown workspace's windows, "Workspace N" said in a toast (compared with Chromium: new same_t.sh cases ws2, ws2-dark, ws2-left; the same steps on both engines: new test iso/qt/native/wsbeh_t.js). Fixed: a notification with no text under its title is as tall as the page's.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 3's last part): the taskbar at the left or the right of the screen, as on Standard: a column as wide as its widest part, the start button, the pinned apps, the open windows one under the other and the tray at the bottom; the desktop's icons, windows, the start menu and the pop-ups placed beside it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: the plan: signed system extensions (Part 13): drivers, firmware and tools added to one computer as signed read-only layers over the unchanged base, instead of a conventional package manager; USB printers (Part 8) are their first use.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 3's last part, first half): the network's pop-up (the adapters, the one in use, Network Settings…); a notification shows in the screen's corner as on Standard (sliding in, gone after its time, a click doing its own action or opening the notifications' centre, ⚡ Why?), not inside the window of the app that sent it, and is in the centre and counted on the bell at once; the taskbar's 🎙️ while an app uses the microphone, muting it for everything with a click (🔇); the bell shows 🔕 with Do not disturb and counts the notifications come since signing in; Meta+N and Meta+A; a setting changed in one app's window reaches the others. Fixed: a dismissed notification could come back for a moment; the shell's dark pop-ups and menus followed the dark theme's switch alone, not the light or dark mode; Settings asked for at a page by another app's window opens at that page.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 3): quick settings (☰: its switches, the network, Lock, Settings, Power) and the notifications' centre (🔔: Do not disturb, Clear all, each notification with its time, ✕ and Blitzen's Why? for a failure), drawn as the desktop page draws them on Standard; the battery's button opens Settings' System health.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 3, second part): the calendar under the taskbar's clock (the month's weeks, today, the Calendar's events and the next four, the months before and after, Open Calendar, a day double-clicked opening the Calendar there) and the volume's pop-up (its slider, Mute, Desktop sounds…), drawn as the desktop page draws them on Standard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 3, first part): the taskbar's right-click menus as the page's, row by row: the taskbar's own (Show desktop, Restore all windows, Cascade windows, Close all windows, Taskbar settings), the start button's, a pinned app's (with each app's own rows: Oracle's New private tab), a window's button's (read from the window's page: Restore, Minimize, Maximize, Always on top, Center on screen, Pin or Unpin, Print / Save as PDF…, Close, Force quit), the sound's, the network's and the clock's (compared with Chromium: new same_t.sh cases tbm-*; the same steps on both engines: new test iso/qt/native/tbbeh_t.js). Fixed: the shell's menus are placed as the page's (above the pointer when they would not fit below); Open Command Prompt opens the page's Command Prompt (terminal).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 2): the desktop's widgets (the clock, the calendar, the sticky note, the system monitor and the weather) drawn by the shell exactly as the page draws them (compared with Chromium: new same_t.sh cases widgets, widgets-ask, widgets-top, widgets-over, widget-picker), each where the account left it: dragged by its header, removed with its ✕, added from the desktop's menu (Add a widget…, the page's picker), the note typed in as the page's textarea (its keys, menu, undo and copy and paste), the weather from Open-Meteo (a click opens Weather), each with the page's timers; saved as the page saves them (bd95widgets, kept by rudolfd until an app's page takes it). The same steps on both engines: new test iso/qt/native/wgbeh_t.js. App windows' pages no longer run the widgets' timers.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 1, second part, drag and drop): a desktop icon follows the pointer as it is dragged; a file dropped on an app's window opens in that app in a window of its own (as the page's __dropFileOnWindow), a file or a shortcut of your own dropped on the Trash goes there; an Explorer window's files dragged onto another window (another page) are dropped there as on Standard (moved between Explorer windows, opened in an app's window). Fixed: on Native each window's page now sees the files the other windows changed (a page that saved tells the others, which read them again), so a window no longer shows or saves back old files. Fixed: an app's window on Native showed its page at the size GTK first asked for (larger than the window, its right and bottom cut off) and was not drawn again where another window uncovered it (the shell's window manager replaced GDK's own X events for its windows); the shell no longer crashes when a window closes while its frame is still there; chosen desktop icons stay chosen when the desktop's list comes again.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 1, second part): the Desktop folder's files and folders as icons in the page's places; the page's right-click menus (the desktop's, a file's, the Trash's, an app's) and its Rename and Open with dialogs drawn by the shell as the page draws them (compared with Chromium: new same_t.sh cases desk-files, desk-menu, file-menu, file-rename, file-openwith); New folder, New text document, Rename (F2), Move to Trash (Delete), Open with, Properties and Empty trash done by the page itself in a hidden one-app window (#app=do-desk, #app=do-fs). Fixed: an app's window or a hidden page no longer squeezes the desktop's icon places into its own size (its grid is the screen's).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: the native desktop (Native engine) now looks as Standard does, measured part by part against the desktop page in Chromium (new test iso/qt/native/same_t.sh, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, "The rule"): the taskbar in its five styles, its buttons' styles and the accent colour's modes (the page's sizes, font, corners, gloss, edges and shadow; the network, sound and battery as the page draws them; the workspaces' buttons; the notifications' count), the desktop's icons (the page's font, wrapping, picture and text shadows), the start menu (the page's own list, with its search box, headings and greyed rows), the windows' frames and title bars in their five styles and colour modes (the page's sizes, round corners, shadow and resize handles; an app's window opens at the page's size and place), and the sign-in and lock screens. Meta+L locks the screen; Start › Shut Down... shows the page's Power dialog.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.6.0 (in progress)
docs.t: New: the native desktop (Native engine, docs/plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, item 1, first part): the desktop's icons, as the page shows them for the account (its shortcuts, pictures and places), on the page's grid at the icon size and display scaling: a double-click opens, dragging moves an icon to the nearest free place (kept by rudolfd), Arrange icons by name, Refresh, and the icon's and the desktop's menus. Files on the desktop come next.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Summary: A native desktop to try (Native, test), Browse with Tor in Oracle, protections against a directed attack, developer mode with custom builds and an official recovery, more memory for games, calls and microphone tests, and Save and Open dialogs with document tabs (docs/plan-1.5.9.md)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: Browse with Tor on Standard: clicking the Tor window's bookmarks bar, address box or buttons no longer jumps back to the desktop, and the Tor window is signed in as the desktop is instead of showing the sign-in screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the self-test run over the read-only development link failed its listeners check when a Linux app was open (it cannot look into other users' programs there); it now says so instead.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Browse with Tor in Oracle: an onion button at the right end of the bookmarks bar sends that window's tabs through Tor, in a private Tor window of its own (Rudolf's Chromium through Tor: sites do not see the computer's address, and no site's name or WebRTC address leaves outside Tor); pressing it again brings the tabs back to a normal window. The window says plainly that this is not Tor Browser's anonymity and links Tor Browser (plan 16.2).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: WordPro's hyperlinks as in other word processors: link to a web address, a place in the document (a heading or a bookmark), a file on this computer or an e-mail address with a subject; the text to show and a ScreenTip; bookmarks; a link's right-click menu (Open, Edit, Copy address, Remove); typed web and e-mail addresses becoming links; and a list of every link with Go to, Edit, Remove and Remove all.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Tor in the system (for Oracle's Browse with Tor, plan 16.1): it runs only while a Tor window is open, as a user of its own, listening only on this computer (127.0.0.1:9050), with nothing kept on the disk; System health notes when it starts, is ready, stops or fails.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the Save As box of Notepad, WordLite, WordPro and Paint (and the Run box) ignored typing: its Enter handler cancelled every other key.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Notepad, WordLite and WordPro save and open through a dialog like the File Explorer: folders, a name, and the file type from a list (Notepad: text, Markdown, web page, Lua, CSV, JSON, batch; WordLite and WordPro: rich document, web page, text). Notepad and WordLite keep several documents in tabs under their buttons (New, Open, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Tab), a file opened from elsewhere joins the open window as a tab, and unsaved tabs are asked about.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: another Rudolf OS stick plugged in (an older one, for example) never showed in the File Explorer: every disk with a Rudolf OS partition was hidden, not only the one Rudolf OS runs from. It now shows; its data partition opens read-only and its start-up parts stay hidden.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Settings › Volume Controls › Microphones has a list of the microphones (the one chosen becomes every app's, a call's too) and a Test button: an equalizer and a level meter show what the chosen microphone hears.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: Oracle on Native (test): a link opened in a new window, Ctrl+N or a web page's file from another app opens an Oracle window of its own, as on Standard, not a window inside Oracle's; closing Oracle while a download is arriving no longer shows Chromium's "Download is in progress" question: the window goes, the download is still put in Downloads and told, then Chromium closes; files saved in Oracle and in an app window that is open are seen by each other at once (before, one could overwrite the other); text copied in Oracle stays on the clipboard after Oracle closes; the volume keys' indicator appears at the top of the screen, not inside a window.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: calls heard nothing on laptops whose built-in microphones are on another sound chip than the speakers (the Vivobook's AMD microphones): the headset jack's microphone was made the default even with nothing plugged in. It is now the default only when a headset is plugged in.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Oracle's bookmarks bar ends with a "+" that adds a bookmark by its address, from the browsing history (newest first, searchable), or as a file on this computer (a document or a PDF).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: choosing a file in the desktop's own file picker (Open a presentation or a spreadsheet, and others) answered as if nothing had been chosen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: the plan: Browse with Tor in Oracle (Part 16): a button on the bookmarks bar sends that window through Tor, which runs only while it is used.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: a USB tethering link or cable without internet took over from a working Wi-Fi, cutting the computer off (found with a MiFi without a data plan on the same network range as the home router). A new wired connection is now used only once the internet answers through it, and is tried again every 30 seconds; until then the Wi-Fi keeps the route and its DNS, and the network menu and Settings say "No internet" for it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Recovery mode in the boot menu now starts its own start-up file, recovery.efi, signed with the Rudolf OS key. It starts only the official recovery system kept on this computer (system/r), after checking that its release list is signed by the official key (never by Developer mode's extra key) and that every file has the size and SHA-256 that list says. A changed or wrongly signed recovery system is refused, with the file and the reason shown, and nothing else is started in its place.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the self-test's listeners check failed while a Linux app ran (the Claude app's own sockets inside Debian, Chromium's newer socket folder), and its Debian check failed when run over the read-only development link; a Linux app's own sockets inside its container are now said as such, and the Debian check says when it cannot look.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: the self-test says which system runs (the Official Rudolf OS, or a Custom build in Developer mode with the key that signed it), and every development link result names the system that answered.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: the development link could not be switched on with the official builds. It needed Developer mode, which can only be turned on by trusting a developer's key. It now has its own switch, "Allow the development link on this computer" (an administrator's password; unticking it ends the link), and Developer mode moved from Update and recovery to Settings › Security, just above the development link.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed (security): the display needs authorization. X no longer lets every program on the computer watch the screen, read the keys and type into the desktop: it starts with a new cookie only root can read, and only root, the desktop's user and the signed-in account's own Linux user may use it (taken back at sign-out). Debian's Linux programs and Wine now run as the signed-in account's own Linux user too, with the account's folder as their home (Wine's programs and their Start menu entries are the account's), and Library packages started from the desktop as well; another account's programs cannot reach them (plan 15.3, second step).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed (security): each account is its own Linux user (uid 1001 and up), made and removed with the account. Its files belong to it alone, and the Linux apps and Flatpak apps it starts run as it, with its own session bus and desktop portal, so one account's apps cannot read another's files; signing out stops all of them. Existing accounts' files are given to their users at the first start (ownership only, logged; what cannot be moved is named in System health). The desktop's page and API now also check the desktop's own user. Debian and Wine follow in the next step.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New (security): the development link can only look at the computer (read files and logs, take screenshots) unless "Allow changes to this computer" is ticked in Settings › Security › Development link, which needs an administrator's password and is unticked again at every start. Read-only is enforced by the system: its commands run as an unprivileged user in a read-only view of the files, without the link's token; bringing files and restarting are refused. The banner says which.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed (security): fewer and harder doors. A list of everything that listens on the computer (TCP ports and Unix sockets), with who may use each and how it checks; the self-test fails when something listens that the list does not name. The system programs are built with the stack protector, FORTIFY_SOURCE=3, PIE, full RELRO and control-flow protection, and each release checks the flags on the built programs. rudolfd's request parsing and JSON are fuzzed before each release; the fuzzing found and fixed a read past the end of a JSON string ending in a broken escape, and a request with a negative or second Content-Length is now refused.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New (security): a daily check compares the Chromium and the kernel of the latest release with the newest ones Ubuntu has published (the chromium snap, Ubuntu's mainline builds of the release's kernel series) and opens one issue "Security update available: …" when either is newer, never a second while one is open; it builds and releases nothing (it replaces the Chromium check). Settings › About shows the release's Chromium and its date.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed (security): the development link is off unless it is being used. It can be switched on only in Developer mode, by an administrator whose password rudolfd now checks itself; Ask first is on again after every restart; the link is off after a restart unless "Keep on after restarting" is ticked (off by default), and turns itself off after 4 hours without a command, with a notification. System health shows whether it is on, since when, who switched it on and its last command.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed (security): WordPro's cleaning of documents and pasted text could be got round (a slash for a space before onerror, an SVG animation, javascript: links), so a crafted document could run script in the desktop. It now uses the browser's own parser (safeHtml) and removes everything that can run. A test opens 19 hostile files in every app; a new check (htmlsinks, run with deadcheck) catches new places that make HTML from data; and the page now forbids plug-in content and outside <base> addresses.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed (security): rudolfd gave the desktop's page, with its API token and the page's stored data, to any program on the computer, so a Linux app, a Wine program or a Flatpak could use the system API, which runs as root. Now the page and the API answer only the desktop's own processes (its memory group) and root; others are refused and System health says so (Security). The kernel also gets Yama, so programs cannot read the browser's memory either. The self-test checks both.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: the plan: on the native desktop, Oracle will run on Chromium with Rudolf's tab shell, as on Standard (real tabs, the same sign-ins and private tabs), started only while Oracle is open (plan Part 12, step 8).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Display Properties says "Note: Dynamic effects are disabled on power-saver mode." under Dynamic Backgrounds, only while power saver (or battery saver) is on, when Spirit Falls' petals and lanterns and Glacier Lake's aurora stand still.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: Rudolf OS's calendars show weeks from Sunday to Saturday (they began on Monday): the Calendar app, the calendar under the taskbar's clock and the calendar widget.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: private browsing in Oracle: New private tab in Oracle's ☰ menu, Ctrl+Shift+N, and when you right-click Oracle's icon (on the taskbar, in the Start menu, on the desktop, or an open Oracle window's taskbar button). A private window is marked 🕶️ Private in dark violet; its pages are not kept in History, its cookies and site data are kept in memory only (with Standard and Lite) and forgotten when the last private window closes; pop-ups from it stay private. Help › Privacy explains what is kept (bookmarks, downloads) and who can still see what you visit.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: the plans: on the native desktop Rudolf OS must appear and work exactly as it does on Standard (Chromium): every part of the native shell, and later every native app, is compared with Standard's in screenshots and behaviour, and each difference is a bug (plan-1.6.0.md Part 12, plan-2.0.md).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: Native (test)'s six bugs seen on the Vivobook (plan 12.3b step 7): a picture of your own shows from the first start (rudolfd makes the shell's copy from the page's database mirror when no page has given it yet); the screen shows the arrow, not X's bare cross; the taskbar follows Display Properties' display scaling and draws the apps' pictures as the page does (not emoji), with the version on the start button; drop-downs in app windows are drawn as in Lite (the page now knows Native's app windows are WebKit); the development link's red banner is drawn once by the shell at the top of the screen (windows kept below it, End now, and it asks about commands itself), no longer inside every app window, where it hid Settings' search box.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Changed: the plans: Rudolf OS goes native (decided from the native engine's measurements on the Vivobook: 854 MB used at idle against Standard's 1,110 MB). Native (test)'s bugs seen on the Vivobook are fixed in 1.5.9 (plan Part 12, step 7); the native shell gets everything the web desktop's shell has and becomes the default in 1.6.0 (plan-1.6.0.md Part 12); the apps are rewritten natively, one by one, for 2.0 (docs/plan-2.0.md).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Settings › System health › Desktop engine › Native (test): the native desktop engine's prototype (plan Part 12), with Lite's safeguards: on trial until its sign-in screen appears, and given up for Standard (said in System health and Settings) after a start that does not get there; never in Recovery mode. Ctrl+Alt+Backspace turns it off too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: the native desktop engine's prototype is a window manager too (plan Part 12): every window gets a title bar in the title bar styles and colours, with minimise, maximise and close, moving and resizing, focus on click, full screen for games and videos, dialogs centred over their window, and the open windows on the taskbar.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: rudolf-native, the native desktop engine's prototype (plan Part 12): the wallpaper, the taskbar in its styles and accent colours, the pinned apps, the tray, the clock, the start menu and the sign-in and lock screens drawn natively (GTK), each app in a WebKit window of its own, all sharing one WebKit process. Not offered in Settings yet.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: rudolfd answers the native desktop engine's questions (plan Part 12): the accounts for its sign-in screen (never a hash), the sign-in itself, checked as the desktop page checks it and opening the account's encrypted folder, and the desktop's settings, pinned apps and start menu; the desktop page gives it the start menu's list and a copy of your own background picture. Written down in docs/api.md.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: the desktop page's one-app mode (for the native desktop engine being prototyped, plan Part 12): index.html#app=NAME starts one app alone, filling the window, signed in from the native session; closing the app writes its files and closes the page.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: Display Properties › Taskbar › Buttons: the taskbar's buttons (start, pinned apps, open windows, workspaces, the tray) in a style of their own (Standard, Wireframe, Monochrome, Candy, Retro), in the accent colour as Normal, Negative or Complementary when "Match the theme colours" is ticked, otherwise in each style's own colours.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: Fixed: plugging in an Android phone with USB debugging or file transfer on no longer says Rudolf OS has no driver for it: apps use those directly, without a driver.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
docs.t: New: the PDF Viewer prints (🖨️ Print, or Ctrl+P): the PDF itself, on its own paper size, to a network printer (IPP Everywhere / AirPrint) or saved as a copy, through the same print dialog as WordPro.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.9 (2026-11-15)
